Mode contract

recorded (outcome.json contract field)

Verbatim, as recorded with the run and sent to the agents.

- primitive to instantiate: `dsp48e2_preadd_ma` (precision INT27)
- what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
- computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
- input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
- output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
- arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on `A`, 25 bits on `D` and 17 bits on `B`; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
- registers: none; the block is combinational, and `P` and `PCOUT` are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
- cascade: `PCOUT` is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. `PCOUT` reaches only the `PCIN` of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. `PCIN` takes only another block's `PCOUT`, or the constant 0.
- tie-off: `PCIN` = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's `PCOUT` or the constant 0 may drive it).
- connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.

element on a pathns
block, input to output2.14
soft flip-flop, clock to output0.060
  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. The block has no reset: "same behavior" must hold after every reset of the design, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original on the testbench's stimulus, which does not respect it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Goal

Propose a correct rewrite onto the block. The loop measures it against the original design on area × delay; you are not asked to predict the result.

Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when you propose no rewrite>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

No rewrite
  • REGIONS: NONE: You propose no rewrite this time. The plan states why, from what you were given: no correct rewrite, or nothing left to try. The run then ends and keeps the best result so far if its median over every seed is below the original's, and the original design otherwise (also when no rewrite has beaten it).
What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left: a correctness reason, or "not chosen this pass"; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the REGIONS line; read the source first.
  • Your reply is read by the framework, not answered by a person, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.
Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output of sv_chip2_hierarchy_no_mem on every cycle after the testbench's reset phase (its first 8 cycles). A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (dsp48e2_preadd_ma.v) are in sim_reference/.

PLAN:

What is rewritten. The seven my_fir_* modules are symmetric FIRs: the coefficient list of each is a palindrome (f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; f2/h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4; f3 12,77,148,0,148,77,12; h1 15,25,193,0,193,25,15; h3/h4 9,56,109,0,109,56,9). Each symmetric pair of taps folds onto one block's pre-adder, (D + A)*B, and the partial sums are accumulated on the P cascade. All 45 listed products are converted; the whole soft adder tree of each module (six 28-bit adds, three of them 28 bits wide at the root) disappears and is replaced by the cascade plus one 28-bit add.

Per-module structure (as in MAPPING): two cascade chains, each at most two blocks deep, and one 28-bit soft add that produces dout. The chain depth is deliberately capped at two blocks: the block is combinational, so a four-block cascade would be a 4 × 2.14 = 8.56 ns combinational path from the tap registers to dout, which is longer than the original mult+adder-tree path; two chains of two give 4.28 ns plus one 28-bit soft add, at the cost of ~28 adder bits per module instance.

Editor instructions.

  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, delete the product/sum expression in the dout <= statement only, and replace it with dout <= sum_a[27:0] + sum_b[27:0]; (for the six-tap modules the same statement; sum_b is then the single-block chain). Leave n_delay_reg1..6, the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) guard, output_data_ready and all ports exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain in f3/h1/h3/h4 even though no block reads it.
  • Declare, at module level, wire [47:0] c0, sum_a, c1, sum_b; (names free) and instantiate the blocks with named port connections .A(...), .D(...), .B(...), .PCIN(...), .P(...), .PCOUT(...) outside the always block. Head block of a chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P() left open, .PCOUT(c0). Tail block: .PCIN(c0), .P(sum_a), .PCOUT() left open. A one-block chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P(sum_b), .PCOUT() open. No PCOUT is read by anything but the next block's PCIN.
  • Zero-extend every tap: .A({11'b0, din}), .D({11'b0, n_delay_reg6}), and so on; the unpaired centre tap of f1/f2/h2 uses .D(27'd0).
  • Do not touch any other module, and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma to stereovision2.v.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned and every coefficient is ≤ 255, so on the block A, D ≤ 2^16−1 (≤ 25 unsigned bits, as required), the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26 so its 27-bit top bit is 0 and it reads as a positive signed number, and B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The widest total is f2/h2: 65535 × (4+42+163+255+163+42+4) = 44,105,055 < 2^28, so every partial sum and the final sum fit far inside the block's 48 bits and inside the 28-bit dout. In the original the products are 32-bit unsigned and the sum is truncated to dout's 28 bits, a truncation that never fires for any input; the rewrite therefore matches bit for bit on every input value, with no assumption about the stimulus. No ASSUMES: line is needed.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products — which nothing else in the design reads — move inside. The pre-adder sums (a+b) are not values of the original design and are not read anywhere.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — operands din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register (clock-enabled by new_data_rdy): one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add, multiply, P-cascade accumulate) → one combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why. The 46 fltr_compute_* products (ids fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134, all seven modules) are not chosen this pass. They are convertible — their coefficients are also palindromic, so the same pair folding applies — but two things make them a poor trade here, not a correctness block: (1) at baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a DSP tile (mult_9x9_fixed_pt, 210 multiplies on 62 tiles), whereas this mode takes a whole tile per block, so converting them would raise the DSP tile count by roughly 88 tiles while removing only a 20-bit adder tree; (2) each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register whose value is then re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so any product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to the sum; with din up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 in fltr_compute_f1 q4, 364 in fltr_compute_f3 q3/q5, 324 in fltr_compute_h4 q4 — and a faithful rewrite would need an added comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term. Together these make the region unattractive relative to the my_fir_* family, which is converted in full. The three * 16'b0000000000000000 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are left as they are.

Resource check. 144 blocks for the my_fir_* family plus the 62 tiles the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies occupy is 206 of the 306 DSP tiles, so the rewrite fits with margin.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic, making the second half of the design's multiplies eligible for this block as well.

2	// as a pre-adder multiply on the P cascade: "C +/- ( B x ( D +/- A ) + W + CIN )" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2)
3	// with AMULTSEL = AD, PREADDINSEL = A, BMULTSEL = B, USE_MULT = MULTIPLY, INMODE = 00100 (D enabled,

5	// CARRYIN = 0, C unused, AREG = BREG = DREG = ADREG = MREG = 0 and PREG = 0. INMODE and OPMODE are fixed
6	// inside the mode. Reference for every per-cycle question: AMD's simulation model
7	// /tools/Xilinx/Vivado/2024.1/data/verilog/src/unisims/DSP48E2.v (Vivado 2024.1; registers start at 0 in the
8	// initial block at lines 1178-1217), read in place and never copied.
9	// P = PCIN + (D + A) * B: the pre-adder sum wraps at 27 bits and is read as signed, the product is
10	// signed 27x18, the sum wraps at 48 bits. No register: P and PCOUT are combinational from A, D, B and PCIN, and PCOUT = P.
11	// PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or 0.
12	// Signed two's complement throughout, as the real block; unsigned data must have a zero top bit on
13	// each operand. Every register starts at 0: AMD's simulation model starts its registers at 0 in the
14	// `initial` block(s) cited below (Vivado 2024.1). Resets are synchronous, active high, clear only the
15	// register(s) they name and win over that register's clock enable. Timing figures and tile area are

19	    input [26:0] D,
20	    input [17:0] B,
21	    input [47:0] PCIN,

24	);

Task

You are the plan reviewer. You did not write this plan. Check it against the design source, the block's contract and the correctness rules; approve it if it violates none.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The block on this architecture

These are read from the architecture file.

element on a pathns
block, input to output2.14
soft flip-flop, clock to output0.060
  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.
The design

The design source is stereovision2.v. The candidate regions the planner was offered:

Multiplies in the unmodified stereovision2, counted in its packed netlist at seed 1: 468 on 236 DSP tiles, of which 258 in two_mult_18x19 mode on 174 tiles (84 tiles with 2 and 90 with 1) and 210 in mult_9x9_fixed_pt mode on 62 tiles (43 tiles with 4, 5 with 3, 9 with 2 and 5 with 1). 546 products in the source become 468 multiply cells after synthesis. The DSP tile count is the same at each of the five seeds. Multiplies in soft logic, if any, are not in this count.

Each row is one multiply of the design as elaborated from the source. An id names it by its module and by the name the elaborated design gives the multiply, which carries the file and the line; multiplies that come from one line (several written on it, or one inside a generate loop) differ in the number after the last $. An operand's bits are the bits it carries, the zero or sign extension to the width of the expression left out; signed or unsigned is how the multiply reads it. Instances is how many instances of the multiply's module the design holds. Nothing else about a multiply is listed: what its product feeds is in the source.

In every row, instances: 6.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. The block has no reset: "same behavior" must hold after every reset of the design, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original on the testbench's stimulus, which does not respect it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left: a correctness reason, or "not chosen this pass"; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically, and your reply is read by the framework, not answered by a person, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

What is rewritten. The seven my_fir_* modules are symmetric FIRs: the coefficient list of each is a palindrome (f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; f2/h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4; f3 12,77,148,0,148,77,12; h1 15,25,193,0,193,25,15; h3/h4 9,56,109,0,109,56,9). Each symmetric pair of taps folds onto one block's pre-adder, (D + A)*B, and the partial sums are accumulated on the P cascade. All 45 listed products are converted; the whole soft adder tree of each module (six 28-bit adds, three of them 28 bits wide at the root) disappears and is replaced by the cascade plus one 28-bit add.

Per-module structure (as in MAPPING): two cascade chains, each at most two blocks deep, and one 28-bit soft add that produces dout. The chain depth is deliberately capped at two blocks: the block is combinational, so a four-block cascade would be a 4 × 2.14 = 8.56 ns combinational path from the tap registers to dout, which is longer than the original mult+adder-tree path; two chains of two give 4.28 ns plus one 28-bit soft add, at the cost of ~28 adder bits per module instance.

Editor instructions.

  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, delete the product/sum expression in the dout <= statement only, and replace it with dout <= sum_a[27:0] + sum_b[27:0]; (for the six-tap modules the same statement; sum_b is then the single-block chain). Leave n_delay_reg1..6, the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) guard, output_data_ready and all ports exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain in f3/h1/h3/h4 even though no block reads it.
  • Declare, at module level, wire [47:0] c0, sum_a, c1, sum_b; (names free) and instantiate the blocks with named port connections .A(...), .D(...), .B(...), .PCIN(...), .P(...), .PCOUT(...) outside the always block. Head block of a chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P() left open, .PCOUT(c0). Tail block: .PCIN(c0), .P(sum_a), .PCOUT() left open. A one-block chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P(sum_b), .PCOUT() open. No PCOUT is read by anything but the next block's PCIN.
  • Zero-extend every tap: .A({11'b0, din}), .D({11'b0, n_delay_reg6}), and so on; the unpaired centre tap of f1/f2/h2 uses .D(27'd0).
  • Do not touch any other module, and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma to stereovision2.v.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned and every coefficient is ≤ 255, so on the block A, D ≤ 2^16−1 (≤ 25 unsigned bits, as required), the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26 so its 27-bit top bit is 0 and it reads as a positive signed number, and B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The widest total is f2/h2: 65535 × (4+42+163+255+163+42+4) = 44,105,055 < 2^28, so every partial sum and the final sum fit far inside the block's 48 bits and inside the 28-bit dout. In the original the products are 32-bit unsigned and the sum is truncated to dout's 28 bits, a truncation that never fires for any input; the rewrite therefore matches bit for bit on every input value, with no assumption about the stimulus. No ASSUMES: line is needed.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products — which nothing else in the design reads — move inside. The pre-adder sums (a+b) are not values of the original design and are not read anywhere.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — operands din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register (clock-enabled by new_data_rdy): one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add, multiply, P-cascade accumulate) → one combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why. The 46 fltr_compute_* products (ids fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134, all seven modules) are not chosen this pass. They are convertible — their coefficients are also palindromic, so the same pair folding applies — but two things make them a poor trade here, not a correctness block: (1) at baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a DSP tile (mult_9x9_fixed_pt, 210 multiplies on 62 tiles), whereas this mode takes a whole tile per block, so converting them would raise the DSP tile count by roughly 88 tiles while removing only a 20-bit adder tree; (2) each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register whose value is then re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so any product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to the sum; with din up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 in fltr_compute_f1 q4, 364 in fltr_compute_f3 q3/q5, 324 in fltr_compute_h4 q4 — and a faithful rewrite would need an added comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term. Together these make the region unattractive relative to the my_fir_* family, which is converted in full. The three * 16'b0000000000000000 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are left as they are.

Resource check. 144 blocks for the my_fir_* family plus the 62 tiles the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies occupy is 206 of the 306 DSP tiles, so the rewrite fits with margin.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic, making the second half of the design's multiplies eligible for this block as well.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output of sv_chip2_hierarchy_no_mem on every cycle after the testbench's reset phase (its first 8 cycles). A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (dsp48e2_preadd_ma.v) are in sim_reference/.

1	// dsp48e2_preadd_ma: behavioural model of the arch mode dsp48e2_preadd_ma_mode, which mimics the AMD DSP48E2 slice
2	// as a pre-adder multiply on the P cascade: "C +/- ( B x ( D +/- A ) + W + CIN )" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2)
3	// with AMULTSEL = AD, PREADDINSEL = A, BMULTSEL = B, USE_MULT = MULTIPLY, INMODE = 00100 (D enabled,
4	// add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000,
5	// CARRYIN = 0, C unused, AREG = BREG = DREG = ADREG = MREG = 0 and PREG = 0. INMODE and OPMODE are fixed
6	// inside the mode. Reference for every per-cycle question: AMD's simulation model
7	// /tools/Xilinx/Vivado/2024.1/data/verilog/src/unisims/DSP48E2.v (Vivado 2024.1; registers start at 0 in the
8	// initial block at lines 1178-1217), read in place and never copied.
9	// P = PCIN + (D + A) * B: the pre-adder sum wraps at 27 bits and is read as signed, the product is
10	// signed 27x18, the sum wraps at 48 bits. No register: P and PCOUT are combinational from A, D, B and PCIN, and PCOUT = P.
11	// PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or 0.
12	// Signed two's complement throughout, as the real block; unsigned data must have a zero top bit on
13	// each operand. Every register starts at 0: AMD's simulation model starts its registers at 0 in the
14	// `initial` block(s) cited below (Vivado 2024.1). Resets are synchronous, active high, clear only the
15	// register(s) they name and win over that register's clock enable. Timing figures and tile area are
16	// this project's arch's own, not AMD's. One block per DSP tile.
17	module dsp48e2_preadd_ma (
18	    input [26:0] A,
19	    input [26:0] D,
20	    input [17:0] B,
21	    input [47:0] PCIN,
22	    output [47:0] P,
23	    output [47:0] PCOUT
24	);
25	    wire [26:0] ad = D + A;                                   // 27-bit pre-adder, wraps
26	    wire signed [44:0] m = $signed(ad) * $signed(B);          // signed 27x18 -> 45, exact
27	    wire [47:0] sum = PCIN + {{3{m[44]}}, m};               // modulo 2^48
28	    assign P = sum;
29	    assign PCOUT = sum;
30	endmodule

  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The block on this architecture

  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.

The plan names their shared sum as 'the dout register of each my_fir_* module (one reduction per module: two PCOUT→PCIN chains joined by a single 28-bit soft add)'.
Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. The block has no reset: "same behavior" must hold after every reset of the design, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original on the testbench's stimulus, which does not respect it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
How to work
  • After each edit, run bash check.sh stereovision2.v and read its output. If it fails, fix the RTL and run it again.
  • check.sh reads the architecture's declaration of every hard block. Instantiate the block by its name and do not declare it in the design: a design that defines a module of the block's name fails the check.
  • Do not run place-and-route or any VTR command; that is done after you finish.
  • Stop when check.sh passes and its cell census shows the block instances the plan calls for.
Output
  • State what you changed, region by region, and stop.
  • Your edit is checked automatically, and this reply is read by the framework, not answered by a person, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

What is rewritten. The seven my_fir_* modules are symmetric FIRs: the coefficient list of each is a palindrome (f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; f2/h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4; f3 12,77,148,0,148,77,12; h1 15,25,193,0,193,25,15; h3/h4 9,56,109,0,109,56,9). Each symmetric pair of taps folds onto one block's pre-adder, (D + A)*B, and the partial sums are accumulated on the P cascade. All 45 listed products are converted; the whole soft adder tree of each module (six 28-bit adds, three of them 28 bits wide at the root) disappears and is replaced by the cascade plus one 28-bit add.

Per-module structure (as in MAPPING): two cascade chains, each at most two blocks deep, and one 28-bit soft add that produces dout. The chain depth is deliberately capped at two blocks: the block is combinational, so a four-block cascade would be a 4 × 2.14 = 8.56 ns combinational path from the tap registers to dout, which is longer than the original mult+adder-tree path; two chains of two give 4.28 ns plus one 28-bit soft add, at the cost of ~28 adder bits per module instance.

Editor instructions.

  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, delete the product/sum expression in the dout <= statement only, and replace it with dout <= sum_a[27:0] + sum_b[27:0]; (for the six-tap modules the same statement; sum_b is then the single-block chain). Leave n_delay_reg1..6, the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) guard, output_data_ready and all ports exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain in f3/h1/h3/h4 even though no block reads it.
  • Declare, at module level, wire [47:0] c0, sum_a, c1, sum_b; (names free) and instantiate the blocks with named port connections .A(...), .D(...), .B(...), .PCIN(...), .P(...), .PCOUT(...) outside the always block. Head block of a chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P() left open, .PCOUT(c0). Tail block: .PCIN(c0), .P(sum_a), .PCOUT() left open. A one-block chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P(sum_b), .PCOUT() open. No PCOUT is read by anything but the next block's PCIN.
  • Zero-extend every tap: .A({11'b0, din}), .D({11'b0, n_delay_reg6}), and so on; the unpaired centre tap of f1/f2/h2 uses .D(27'd0).
  • Do not touch any other module, and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma to stereovision2.v.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned and every coefficient is ≤ 255, so on the block A, D ≤ 2^16−1 (≤ 25 unsigned bits, as required), the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26 so its 27-bit top bit is 0 and it reads as a positive signed number, and B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The widest total is f2/h2: 65535 × (4+42+163+255+163+42+4) = 44,105,055 < 2^28, so every partial sum and the final sum fit far inside the block's 48 bits and inside the 28-bit dout. In the original the products are 32-bit unsigned and the sum is truncated to dout's 28 bits, a truncation that never fires for any input; the rewrite therefore matches bit for bit on every input value, with no assumption about the stimulus. No ASSUMES: line is needed.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products — which nothing else in the design reads — move inside. The pre-adder sums (a+b) are not values of the original design and are not read anywhere.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — operands din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register (clock-enabled by new_data_rdy): one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add, multiply, P-cascade accumulate) → one combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why. The 46 fltr_compute_* products (ids fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134, all seven modules) are not chosen this pass. They are convertible — their coefficients are also palindromic, so the same pair folding applies — but two things make them a poor trade here, not a correctness block: (1) at baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a DSP tile (mult_9x9_fixed_pt, 210 multiplies on 62 tiles), whereas this mode takes a whole tile per block, so converting them would raise the DSP tile count by roughly 88 tiles while removing only a 20-bit adder tree; (2) each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register whose value is then re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so any product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to the sum; with din up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 in fltr_compute_f1 q4, 364 in fltr_compute_f3 q3/q5, 324 in fltr_compute_h4 q4 — and a faithful rewrite would need an added comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term. Together these make the region unattractive relative to the my_fir_* family, which is converted in full. The three * 16'b0000000000000000 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are left as they are.

Resource check. 144 blocks for the my_fir_* family plus the 62 tiles the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies occupy is 206 of the 306 DSP tiles, so the rewrite fits with margin.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output of sv_chip2_hierarchy_no_mem on every cycle after the testbench's reset phase (its first 8 cycles), on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (dsp48e2_preadd_ma.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

// dsp48e2_preadd_ma: behavioural model of the arch mode dsp48e2_preadd_ma_mode, which mimics the AMD DSP48E2 slice
// as a pre-adder multiply on the P cascade: "C +/- ( B x ( D +/- A ) + W + CIN )" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2)
// with AMULTSEL = AD, PREADDINSEL = A, BMULTSEL = B, USE_MULT = MULTIPLY, INMODE = 00100 (D enabled,
// add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000,
// CARRYIN = 0, C unused, AREG = BREG = DREG = ADREG = MREG = 0 and PREG = 0. INMODE and OPMODE are fixed
// inside the mode. Reference for every per-cycle question: AMD's simulation model
// /tools/Xilinx/Vivado/2024.1/data/verilog/src/unisims/DSP48E2.v (Vivado 2024.1; registers start at 0 in the
// initial block at lines 1178-1217), read in place and never copied.
// P = PCIN + (D + A) * B: the pre-adder sum wraps at 27 bits and is read as signed, the product is
// signed 27x18, the sum wraps at 48 bits. No register: P and PCOUT are combinational from A, D, B and PCIN, and PCOUT = P.
// PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or 0.
// Signed two's complement throughout, as the real block; unsigned data must have a zero top bit on
// each operand. Every register starts at 0: AMD's simulation model starts its registers at 0 in the
// `initial` block(s) cited below (Vivado 2024.1). Resets are synchronous, active high, clear only the
// register(s) they name and win over that register's clock enable. Timing figures and tile area are
// this project's arch's own, not AMD's. One block per DSP tile.
module dsp48e2_preadd_ma (
    input [26:0] A,
    input [26:0] D,
    input [17:0] B,
    input [47:0] PCIN,
    output [47:0] P,
    output [47:0] PCOUT
);
    wire [26:0] ad = D + A;                                   // 27-bit pre-adder, wraps
    wire signed [44:0] m = $signed(ad) * $signed(B);          // signed 27x18 -> 45, exact
    wire [47:0] sum = PCIN + {{3{m[44]}}, m};               // modulo 2^48
    assign P = sum;
    assign PCOUT = sum;
endmodule

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.

PLAN:

What is rewritten. The seven my_fir_* modules are symmetric FIRs: the coefficient list of each is a palindrome (f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; f2/h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4; f3 12,77,148,0,148,77,12; h1 15,25,193,0,193,25,15; h3/h4 9,56,109,0,109,56,9). Each symmetric pair of taps folds onto one block's pre-adder, (D + A)*B, and the partial sums are accumulated on the P cascade. All 45 listed products are converted; the whole soft adder tree of each module (six 28-bit adds, three of them 28 bits wide at the root) disappears and is replaced by the cascade plus one 28-bit add.

Per-module structure (as in MAPPING): two cascade chains, each at most two blocks deep, and one 28-bit soft add that produces dout. The chain depth is deliberately capped at two blocks: the block is combinational, so a four-block cascade would be a 4 × 2.14 = 8.56 ns combinational path from the tap registers to dout, which is longer than the original mult+adder-tree path; two chains of two give 4.28 ns plus one 28-bit soft add, at the cost of ~28 adder bits per module instance.

Editor instructions.

  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, delete the product/sum expression in the dout <= statement only, and replace it with dout <= sum_a[27:0] + sum_b[27:0]; (for the six-tap modules the same statement; sum_b is then the single-block chain). Leave n_delay_reg1..6, the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) guard, output_data_ready and all ports exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain in f3/h1/h3/h4 even though no block reads it.
  • Declare, at module level, wire [47:0] c0, sum_a, c1, sum_b; (names free) and instantiate the blocks with named port connections .A(...), .D(...), .B(...), .PCIN(...), .P(...), .PCOUT(...) outside the always block. Head block of a chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P() left open, .PCOUT(c0). Tail block: .PCIN(c0), .P(sum_a), .PCOUT() left open. A one-block chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P(sum_b), .PCOUT() open. No PCOUT is read by anything but the next block's PCIN.
  • Zero-extend every tap: .A({11'b0, din}), .D({11'b0, n_delay_reg6}), and so on; the unpaired centre tap of f1/f2/h2 uses .D(27'd0).
  • Do not touch any other module, and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma to stereovision2.v.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned and every coefficient is ≤ 255, so on the block A, D ≤ 2^16−1 (≤ 25 unsigned bits, as required), the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26 so its 27-bit top bit is 0 and it reads as a positive signed number, and B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The widest total is f2/h2: 65535 × (4+42+163+255+163+42+4) = 44,105,055 < 2^28, so every partial sum and the final sum fit far inside the block's 48 bits and inside the 28-bit dout. In the original the products are 32-bit unsigned and the sum is truncated to dout's 28 bits, a truncation that never fires for any input; the rewrite therefore matches bit for bit on every input value, with no assumption about the stimulus. No ASSUMES: line is needed.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products — which nothing else in the design reads — move inside. The pre-adder sums (a+b) are not values of the original design and are not read anywhere.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — operands din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register (clock-enabled by new_data_rdy): one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add, multiply, P-cascade accumulate) → one combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why. The 46 fltr_compute_* products (ids fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134, all seven modules) are not chosen this pass. They are convertible — their coefficients are also palindromic, so the same pair folding applies — but two things make them a poor trade here, not a correctness block: (1) at baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a DSP tile (mult_9x9_fixed_pt, 210 multiplies on 62 tiles), whereas this mode takes a whole tile per block, so converting them would raise the DSP tile count by roughly 88 tiles while removing only a 20-bit adder tree; (2) each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register whose value is then re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so any product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to the sum; with din up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 in fltr_compute_f1 q4, 364 in fltr_compute_f3 q3/q5, 324 in fltr_compute_h4 q4 — and a faithful rewrite would need an added comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term. Together these make the region unattractive relative to the my_fir_* family, which is converted in full. The three * 16'b0000000000000000 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are left as they are.

Resource check. 144 blocks for the my_fir_* family plus the 62 tiles the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies occupy is 206 of the 306 DSP tiles, so the rewrite fits with margin.

I'll read the source and the supporting files.

ACCEPT

Checked against the plan, the block contract, and the correctness rules.

Plan conformance

  • 24 instantiations in the source (f1 4, f2 4, f3 3, h1 3, h2 4, h3 3, h4 3), matching MAPPING exactly: stereovision2.v:1477-1488, 1543-1554, 1613-1621, 1680-1688, 1743-1754, 1812-1820, 1878-1886. h_fltr is instantiated 6× (188-197), so 144 blocks as planned; 144 + 62 untouched tiles = 206 ≤ 306.
  • Changes are confined to the seven my_fir_* modules: added wire declarations, block instances, and the replacement dout <= sum_a[27:0] + sum_b[27:0]; (1502, 1568, 1635, 1702, 1768, 1834, 1900). The delay chain, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, ports and n_delay_reg3 (kept in f3/h1/h3/h4) are untouched; remaining diff hunks are trailing-whitespace only. No dsp48e2_preadd_ma module definition was added.

Ports and cascade

  • Every input port is connected on every instance: A, D, B, PCIN. Heads use .PCIN(48'd0) with .P() open and .PCOUT(c0/c1); tails use .PCIN(c0/c1), .P(sum_a/sum_b), .PCOUT() open; single-block chains use .PCIN(48'd0), .P(sum_b). c0/c1 are each read only by the next block's PCIN — no other reader, so the dedicated-wire rule holds. Chain depth is 2, as planned.

Arithmetic and equivalence

  • Taps are 16-bit unsigned, zero-extended {11'b0, …} to the 27-bit ports (≤ 25 unsigned bits, within the limit); D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so the 27-bit pre-adder sum has a zero top bit and reads as positive signed; B ≤ 255 (zero top bit).
  • Coefficient folding matches the originals term for term, including the unpaired centre taps (D(27'd0) with B=235 in f1, B=255 in f2/h2) and the omitted zero-coefficient n_delay_reg3 term in f3/h1/h3/h4.
  • Worst case (f2/h2) is 65535×673 = 44,105,055 < 2^28, so neither the 48-bit cascade nor the 28-bit dout truncation ever fires; the fold is exact over the integers on every input, so no ASSUMES: line is needed, consistent with the plan.

Visibility, registers, reset

  • Only the products move inside the blocks; nothing else in the design reads them. din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their registers and remain readable outside.
  • The blocks are combinational and the edit adds no registers, so the single dout register stage and its enable are unchanged, and behaviour after any reset of the design is unaffected (these registers have no reset in the original either).

1	// dsp48e2_preadd_ma: behavioural model of the arch mode dsp48e2_preadd_ma_mode, which mimics the AMD DSP48E2 slice
2	// as a pre-adder multiply on the P cascade: "C +/- ( B x ( D +/- A ) + W + CIN )" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2)
3	// with AMULTSEL = AD, PREADDINSEL = A, BMULTSEL = B, USE_MULT = MULTIPLY, INMODE = 00100 (D enabled,
4	// add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000,
5	// CARRYIN = 0, C unused, AREG = BREG = DREG = ADREG = MREG = 0 and PREG = 0. INMODE and OPMODE are fixed
6	// inside the mode. Reference for every per-cycle question: AMD's simulation model
7	// /tools/Xilinx/Vivado/2024.1/data/verilog/src/unisims/DSP48E2.v (Vivado 2024.1; registers start at 0 in the
8	// initial block at lines 1178-1217), read in place and never copied.
9	// P = PCIN + (D + A) * B: the pre-adder sum wraps at 27 bits and is read as signed, the product is
10	// signed 27x18, the sum wraps at 48 bits. No register: P and PCOUT are combinational from A, D, B and PCIN, and PCOUT = P.
11	// PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or 0.
12	// Signed two's complement throughout, as the real block; unsigned data must have a zero top bit on
13	// each operand. Every register starts at 0: AMD's simulation model starts its registers at 0 in the
14	// `initial` block(s) cited below (Vivado 2024.1). Resets are synchronous, active high, clear only the
15	// register(s) they name and win over that register's clock enable. Timing figures and tile area are
16	// this project's arch's own, not AMD's. One block per DSP tile.
17	module dsp48e2_preadd_ma (
18	    input [26:0] A,
19	    input [26:0] D,
20	    input [17:0] B,
21	    input [47:0] PCIN,
22	    output [47:0] P,
23	    output [47:0] PCOUT
24	);
25	    wire [26:0] ad = D + A;                                   // 27-bit pre-adder, wraps
26	    wire signed [44:0] m = $signed(ad) * $signed(B);          // signed 27x18 -> 45, exact
27	    wire [47:0] sum = PCIN + {{3{m[44]}}, m};               // modulo 2^48
28	    assign P = sum;
29	    assign PCOUT = sum;
30	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The block on this architecture

These are read from the architecture file.

element on a pathns
block, input to output2.14
soft flip-flop, clock to output0.060
  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. The block has no reset: "same behavior" must hold after every reset of the design, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original on the testbench's stimulus, which does not respect it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Goal

Propose a correct rewrite onto the block. The loop measures it against the original design on area × delay; you are not asked to predict the result.

Output
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when you propose no rewrite>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

No rewrite
  • REGIONS: NONE: You propose no rewrite this time. The plan states why, from what you were given: no correct rewrite, or nothing left to try. The run then ends and keeps the best result so far if its median over every seed is below the original's, and the original design otherwise (also when no rewrite has beaten it).
What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left: a correctness reason, or "not chosen this pass"; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the REGIONS line; read the source first.
  • Your reply is read by the framework, not answered by a person, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

PLAN:

What is rewritten. The seven my_fir_* modules are symmetric FIRs: the coefficient list of each is a palindrome (f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; f2/h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4; f3 12,77,148,0,148,77,12; h1 15,25,193,0,193,25,15; h3/h4 9,56,109,0,109,56,9). Each symmetric pair of taps folds onto one block's pre-adder, (D + A)*B, and the partial sums are accumulated on the P cascade. All 45 listed products are converted; the whole soft adder tree of each module (six 28-bit adds, three of them 28 bits wide at the root) disappears and is replaced by the cascade plus one 28-bit add.

Per-module structure (as in MAPPING): two cascade chains, each at most two blocks deep, and one 28-bit soft add that produces dout. The chain depth is deliberately capped at two blocks: the block is combinational, so a four-block cascade would be a 4 × 2.14 = 8.56 ns combinational path from the tap registers to dout, which is longer than the original mult+adder-tree path; two chains of two give 4.28 ns plus one 28-bit soft add, at the cost of ~28 adder bits per module instance.

Editor instructions.

  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, delete the product/sum expression in the dout <= statement only, and replace it with dout <= sum_a[27:0] + sum_b[27:0]; (for the six-tap modules the same statement; sum_b is then the single-block chain). Leave n_delay_reg1..6, the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) guard, output_data_ready and all ports exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain in f3/h1/h3/h4 even though no block reads it.
  • Declare, at module level, wire [47:0] c0, sum_a, c1, sum_b; (names free) and instantiate the blocks with named port connections .A(...), .D(...), .B(...), .PCIN(...), .P(...), .PCOUT(...) outside the always block. Head block of a chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P() left open, .PCOUT(c0). Tail block: .PCIN(c0), .P(sum_a), .PCOUT() left open. A one-block chain: .PCIN(48'd0), .P(sum_b), .PCOUT() open. No PCOUT is read by anything but the next block's PCIN.
  • Zero-extend every tap: .A({11'b0, din}), .D({11'b0, n_delay_reg6}), and so on; the unpaired centre tap of f1/f2/h2 uses .D(27'd0).
  • Do not touch any other module, and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma to stereovision2.v.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned and every coefficient is ≤ 255, so on the block A, D ≤ 2^16−1 (≤ 25 unsigned bits, as required), the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26 so its 27-bit top bit is 0 and it reads as a positive signed number, and B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The widest total is f2/h2: 65535 × (4+42+163+255+163+42+4) = 44,105,055 < 2^28, so every partial sum and the final sum fit far inside the block's 48 bits and inside the 28-bit dout. In the original the products are 32-bit unsigned and the sum is truncated to dout's 28 bits, a truncation that never fires for any input; the rewrite therefore matches bit for bit on every input value, with no assumption about the stimulus. No ASSUMES: line is needed.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products — which nothing else in the design reads — move inside. The pre-adder sums (a+b) are not values of the original design and are not read anywhere.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — operands din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register (clock-enabled by new_data_rdy): one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add, multiply, P-cascade accumulate) → one combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why. The 46 fltr_compute_* products (ids fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134, all seven modules) are not chosen this pass. They are convertible — their coefficients are also palindromic, so the same pair folding applies — but two things make them a poor trade here, not a correctness block: (1) at baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a DSP tile (mult_9x9_fixed_pt, 210 multiplies on 62 tiles), whereas this mode takes a whole tile per block, so converting them would raise the DSP tile count by roughly 88 tiles while removing only a 20-bit adder tree; (2) each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register whose value is then re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so any product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to the sum; with din up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 in fltr_compute_f1 q4, 364 in fltr_compute_f3 q3/q5, 324 in fltr_compute_h4 q4 — and a faithful rewrite would need an added comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term. Together these make the region unattractive relative to the my_fir_* family, which is converted in full. The three * 16'b0000000000000000 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are left as they are.

Resource check. 144 blocks for the my_fir_* family plus the 62 tiles the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies occupy is 206 of the 306 DSP tiles, so the rewrite fits with margin.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic, making the second half of the design's multiplies eligible for this block as well.

PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate. The kept candidate folds each symmetric FIR pair onto the pre-adder (that part is kept unchanged) and then accumulates the partial products on the P cascade. The measured critical path shows the cascade is the expensive part: the hop PCOUT → PCIN costs 2.358 ns of wire plus 2.140 ns of the second block, 4.50 ns, where one level of soft 28-bit add on the same path costs 1.481 ns of wire plus 0.752 ns of carry chain, 2.23 ns. This pass therefore drops the cascade entirely: every block is a leaf with PCIN = 48'd0, and the per-module reduction becomes a two-level soft adder tree. Expected path, from the same start as the measured one: 0.103 (tap flop) + 1.417 (wire to A) + 2.140 (block) + 2.23 (add level 1) + ~2.15 (add level 2) + 1.44 (the new_data_rdy enable mux on dout) ≈ 9.5 ns against the measured 11.84 ns, at the cost of one or two extra 28-bit adders per module instance.

Second change: in my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 the outer pair has coefficient 4, so its folded product (din + n_delay_reg6) * 4 is a pure bit shift. It is left in soft logic as {s0, 2'b00} with s0 = {1'b0,din} + {1'b0,n_delay_reg6} (17 bits, no wrap: 2*65535 = 131070 < 2^17). That removes one whole DSP tile (253779 area units, about nine CLBs) per instance of those two modules, 12 tiles in all, and the shifted term also reaches the adder tree earlier than a block product does. Block count falls from 144 to 132.

Per-module structure (as in MAPPING): four leaves in f1 (blocks ×29, ×101, ×15, ×235) reduced as (p0+p1) + (p2+p3); four leaves in f2 and h2 (blocks ×42, ×163, ×255 plus the shifted ×4 pair) reduced as (p1+p2) + (p3 + shift); three leaves in f3, h1, h3, h4 reduced as (p0+p1) + p2. Every leaf is therefore at most two add levels from dout, and the three-leaf form is no slower than the four-leaf one since all block leaves arrive at the same time.

  • Work from the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory; the kept candidate's edit is not present in it.
  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, replace only the dout <= ... product-sum statement inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) with the single statement given in MAPPING. Leave n_delay_reg1..6, the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list and the COEF* defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though no block reads it.
  • Declare at module level wire [47:0] p0, p1, p2, p3; (only the ones used; names free) and, in f2 and h2 only, wire [16:0] s0; assign s0 = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};.
  • Instantiate the blocks outside the always block with named connections: .A({11'b0, <tap>}), .D({11'b0, <tap>}), .B(18'd<c>), .PCIN(48'd0), .P(pN), .PCOUT(). The unpaired centre tap of f1/f2/h2 uses .D(27'd0). Every input port is connected; PCIN is tied to the constant 0 on every block, which is permitted for a block that is not cascaded; no PCOUT is read.
  • Do not touch any other module, and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma to stereovision2.v.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned and every coefficient is at most 255, so A, D ≤ 65535 (within the 25 unsigned bits the block allows), the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26 so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and it reads as a positive signed value, and B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c. The ×4 pair left in soft logic is the same identity followed by a shift, (din + n_delay_reg6) * 4 = {din + n_delay_reg6, 2'b00}, computed in 17+2 bits with no wrap.
  • The widest module total is f2/h2: 65535 × (4+42+163+255+163+42+4) = 44,105,055 < 2^28, so every leaf, every partial sum of the tree and the final sum fit inside 28 bits and far inside the blocks' 48 bits. In the original the products are unsigned and the sum is assigned to the 28-bit dout, a truncation that can never fire. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads, move inside. The pre-adder sums are not values of the original design. PCOUT drives nothing.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add and multiply) → two levels of combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why.

  • my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1542$169, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1716$210, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1722$221 (the four ×4 taps): deliberately not converted this pass. Multiplying by 4 is a bit shift, so a whole DSP tile would buy nothing; their folded pair is computed in soft logic as a 17-bit add and a shift, which is both smaller and faster than a block. Their arithmetic is still kept exactly, as a term of the same sum.
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (ids fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for the same two reasons as before, neither of them a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding them (25 blocks per instance set, 150 blocks) would add about 88 DSP tiles, roughly +22e6 area units, while removing only a 20-bit adder tree worth a small fraction of that — and 132 + 150 = 282 of 306 tiles leaves very little placement room. (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term, plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline into a registered-din stage. The three * 16'b0...0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 132 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in the kept candidate's measurement) is under 200 of the 306 DSP tiles, 12 fewer than the kept candidate.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would also become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family.
