PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate. The kept candidate folds each symmetric FIR pair onto the pre-adder (that part is kept unchanged) and then accumulates the partial products on the P cascade. The measured critical path shows the cascade is the expensive part: the hop PCOUT → PCIN costs 2.358 ns of wire plus 2.140 ns of the second block, 4.50 ns, where one level of soft 28-bit add on the same path costs 1.481 ns of wire plus 0.752 ns of carry chain, 2.23 ns. This pass therefore drops the cascade entirely: every block is a leaf with PCIN = 48'd0, and the per-module reduction becomes a two-level soft adder tree. Expected path, from the same start as the measured one: 0.103 (tap flop) + 1.417 (wire to A) + 2.140 (block) + 2.23 (add level 1) + ~2.15 (add level 2) + 1.44 (the new_data_rdy enable mux on dout) ≈ 9.5 ns against the measured 11.84 ns, at the cost of one or two extra 28-bit adders per module instance.

Second change: in my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 the outer pair has coefficient 4, so its folded product (din + n_delay_reg6) * 4 is a pure bit shift. It is left in soft logic as {s0, 2'b00} with s0 = {1'b0,din} + {1'b0,n_delay_reg6} (17 bits, no wrap: 2*65535 = 131070 < 2^17). That removes one whole DSP tile (253779 area units, about nine CLBs) per instance of those two modules, 12 tiles in all, and the shifted term also reaches the adder tree earlier than a block product does. Block count falls from 144 to 132.

Per-module structure (as in MAPPING): four leaves in f1 (blocks ×29, ×101, ×15, ×235) reduced as (p0+p1) + (p2+p3); four leaves in f2 and h2 (blocks ×42, ×163, ×255 plus the shifted ×4 pair) reduced as (p1+p2) + (p3 + shift); three leaves in f3, h1, h3, h4 reduced as (p0+p1) + p2. Every leaf is therefore at most two add levels from dout, and the three-leaf form is no slower than the four-leaf one since all block leaves arrive at the same time.

Editor instructions.

  • Work from the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory; the kept candidate's edit is not present in it.
  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, replace only the dout <= ... product-sum statement inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) with the single statement given in MAPPING. Leave n_delay_reg1..6, the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list and the COEF* defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though no block reads it.
  • Declare at module level wire [47:0] p0, p1, p2, p3; (only the ones used; names free) and, in f2 and h2 only, wire [16:0] s0; assign s0 = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};.
  • Instantiate the blocks outside the always block with named connections: .A({11'b0, <tap>}), .D({11'b0, <tap>}), .B(18'd<c>), .PCIN(48'd0), .P(pN), .PCOUT(). The unpaired centre tap of f1/f2/h2 uses .D(27'd0). Every input port is connected; PCIN is tied to the constant 0 on every block, which is permitted for a block that is not cascaded; no PCOUT is read.
  • Do not touch any other module, and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma to stereovision2.v.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned and every coefficient is at most 255, so A, D ≤ 65535 (within the 25 unsigned bits the block allows), the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26 so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and it reads as a positive signed value, and B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c. The ×4 pair left in soft logic is the same identity followed by a shift, (din + n_delay_reg6) * 4 = {din + n_delay_reg6, 2'b00}, computed in 17+2 bits with no wrap.
  • The widest module total is f2/h2: 65535 × (4+42+163+255+163+42+4) = 44,105,055 < 2^28, so every leaf, every partial sum of the tree and the final sum fit inside 28 bits and far inside the blocks' 48 bits. In the original the products are unsigned and the sum is assigned to the 28-bit dout, a truncation that can never fire. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads, move inside. The pre-adder sums are not values of the original design. PCOUT drives nothing.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add and multiply) → two levels of combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why.

  • my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1542$169, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1716$210, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1722$221 (the four ×4 taps): deliberately not converted this pass. Multiplying by 4 is a bit shift, so a whole DSP tile would buy nothing; their folded pair is computed in soft logic as a 17-bit add and a shift, which is both smaller and faster than a block. Their arithmetic is still kept exactly, as a term of the same sum.
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (ids fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for the same two reasons as before, neither of them a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding them (25 blocks per instance set, 150 blocks) would add about 88 DSP tiles, roughly +22e6 area units, while removing only a 20-bit adder tree worth a small fraction of that — and 132 + 150 = 282 of 306 tiles leaves very little placement room. (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term, plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline into a registered-din stage. The three * 16'b0...0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 132 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in the kept candidate's measurement) is under 200 of the 306 DSP tiles, 12 fewer than the kept candidate.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would also become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family.

PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate (revision 1). Revision 1 put every folded symmetric pair on a block: 132 blocks, measured 8.286 ns and 8.204e7 area, product 6.80e8. Its measured path shows where the time goes: 1.940 ns of wire from the tap flop to A, 2.140 ns of block, then 1.504 ns for the first 28-bit add (0.752 wire + 0.752 chain), 0.861 ns for the second, and 1.752 ns for the new_data_rdy enable mux at dout. Two facts follow. First, more than half the period (5.08 ns of 8.29) is routing wire, so shrinking the placement is the main remaining delay lever, and DSP tiles are what spread it: a block tile is 253779 area units, 9.1 CLBs. Second, a soft carry-chain level costs ~1.5 ns from its driver, so a folded product whose coefficient needs exactly one add/subtract of two shifted copies of the pair sum reaches the tree at ~2.9 ns — well before a block product's 4.18 ns — while costing two small adders instead of a whole tile.

This pass therefore keeps on the block exactly those folded products whose coefficient is expensive in soft logic (three or more non-zero CSD terms, i.e. two or more chained adders after the pair sum: 29, 101, 235, 42, 163, 77, 148, 25, 193, 109) and computes outside the block the folded products whose coefficient is a single shift-add (15, 12, 9, 56, 255, and the ×4 already left soft in revision 1). Those terms gain nothing from a 2.14 ns multiplier and a whole tile. The pre-adder folding itself, the per-module reduction depth and every register are unchanged from revision 1, so this is a strict area reduction with no structural risk: blocks fall from 132 to 78, i.e. 54 DSP tiles (1.37e7 area units) removed against roughly 96 added adders of about 22 bits (~2100 adder bits over all 42 module instances, on the order of 3e6 area units). The reduction trees keep the same depth for the block leaves in f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, and h3/h4 improve from depth 2 to depth 1 for their block leaf, so the period should not regress and the h3/h4 paths get shorter.

Per-module leaf arrival and tree shape (as in MAPPING). f1 has four leaves (blocks ×29, ×101, ×235 and soft ×15), reduced balanced at depth 2, exactly as revision 1's f1. f2/h2 have four leaves (blocks ×42, ×163 and soft ×4, ×255), depth 2. f3 and h1 have three leaves (two blocks, one soft), depth 2. h3/h4 have three leaves (one block ×109, soft ×9 and ×56), reduced as p + (t9 + t56) so the block product passes through a single adder.

Editor instructions.

  • Work from the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory; the kept candidate's edit is not present in it. Do not edit any other file and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma.
  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, replace only the dout <= ... product-sum statement inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) with the single statement given in MAPPING. Leave the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list, the register declarations and all COEF* defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though nothing reads it there, as in the original.
  • At module level declare wire [47:0] p0, p1, p2, p3; (only the ones that module uses; names free) and the soft wires listed in MAPPING with exactly the widths given, as continuous assigns. Do not narrow or widen them: the widths are chosen so no intermediate wraps.
  • Instantiate the blocks outside the always block, with named connections only: .A({11'b0, <tap>}), .D({11'b0, <tap>}), .B(18'd<c>), .PCIN(48'd0), .P(pN), .PCOUT(). The unpaired centre taps (f1 ×235) use .D(27'd0). Every input port is connected; PCIN is tied to the constant 0 on every block, permitted for a block that is not cascaded; no PCOUT is read.
  • Touch no other module.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned (WIDTH_5B = 16) and every coefficient is at most 255, so on each block A, D ≤ 65535, inside the 25 unsigned bits the block allows; the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and the sum reads as a positive signed value; B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The soft terms are the same identity followed by one shift-add, each sized to its exact range: t4 = 4·s0 ≤ 524280 < 2^19; t9 = 9·s0 ≤ 1179630 < 2^21; t12 = 12·s0 ≤ 1572840 < 2^21; t15 = 16·s − s with 16·s ≤ 2097120 < 2^21 and the difference non-negative; t56 = 64·s1 − 8·s1 with 64·s1 ≤ 8388480 < 2^23; t255 = 256·x3 − x3 with 256·x3 ≤ 16776960 < 2^24. No intermediate shift and no subtraction overflows or borrows, and every result is non-negative.
  • Module totals: f1 65535·525 = 34.4M, f2/h2 65535·673 = 44.1M, f3 65535·474, h1 65535·466, h3/h4 65535·348 — all below 2^28, so every leaf, every partial sum and the final sum fit in the 28-bit dout and far inside the blocks' 48 bits. In the original the sum is likewise assigned to the 28-bit dout, a truncation that can never fire. All wires are unsigned, so every addend is zero-extended to the 28-bit context of the dout assignment. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads, move inside a block. The pre-adder sums are not values of the original design. PCOUT drives nothing.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add and multiply) in parallel with combinational soft pair-adds and shift-adds → one or two levels of combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why.

  • Left because the folded pair's coefficient is a single shift-add, so a whole DSP tile (9.1 CLBs) would buy nothing and the soft term also reaches the reduction earlier than a block product does; their arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same sum: my_fir_f1.$mul$…1488$157 and …1490$161 (×15), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1542$169, …1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1716$210, …1722$221 (×4), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1545$174, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1719$215 (×255, an unpaired centre tap: one 24-bit subtract), my_fir_f3.$mul$…1602$184, …1607$193 (×12), my_fir_h1.$mul$…1661$197, …1666$206 (×15), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1775$225, …1780$234, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1833$238, …1838$247 (×9), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1776$226, …1779$232, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1834$239, …1837$245 (×56).
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for two reasons, neither a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding them (25 blocks per instance set, 150 blocks) would add roughly 88 DSP tiles, about +2.2e7 area units, while removing only a 20-bit adder tree worth a small fraction of that — the opposite of this pass's direction. (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 78 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in revision 1) is about 135 of the 306 DSP tiles, 56 fewer than revision 1's 191 — the compaction that should also shorten the 1.94 ns flop-to-A route.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would also become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output of sv_chip2_hierarchy_no_mem on every cycle after the testbench's reset phase (its first 8 cycles). A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (dsp48e2_preadd_ma.v) are in sim_reference/.

Task

Edit stereovision2.v in this directory to carry out the approved plan below: rewrite the regions it names onto the hard block described next. If a step cannot be done as the plan says, stop and say which step and why; do not improvise a different rewrite.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The block on this architecture

These are read from the architecture file.

block, input to output2.14
soft flip-flop, clock to output0.060
  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.

PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate (revision 1). Revision 1 put every folded symmetric pair on a block: 132 blocks, measured 8.286 ns and 8.204e7 area, product 6.80e8. Its measured path shows where the time goes: 1.940 ns of wire from the tap flop to A, 2.140 ns of block, then 1.504 ns for the first 28-bit add (0.752 wire + 0.752 chain), 0.861 ns for the second, and 1.752 ns for the new_data_rdy enable mux at dout. Two facts follow. First, more than half the period (5.08 ns of 8.29) is routing wire, so shrinking the placement is the main remaining delay lever, and DSP tiles are what spread it: a block tile is 253779 area units, 9.1 CLBs. Second, a soft carry-chain level costs ~1.5 ns from its driver, so a folded product whose coefficient needs exactly one add/subtract of two shifted copies of the pair sum reaches the tree at ~2.9 ns — well before a block product's 4.18 ns — while costing two small adders instead of a whole tile.

This pass therefore keeps on the block exactly those folded products whose coefficient is expensive in soft logic (three or more non-zero CSD terms, i.e. two or more chained adders after the pair sum: 29, 101, 235, 42, 163, 77, 148, 25, 193, 109) and computes outside the block the folded products whose coefficient is a single shift-add (15, 12, 9, 56, 255, and the ×4 already left soft in revision 1). Those terms gain nothing from a 2.14 ns multiplier and a whole tile. The pre-adder folding itself, the per-module reduction depth and every register are unchanged from revision 1, so this is a strict area reduction with no structural risk: blocks fall from 132 to 78, i.e. 54 DSP tiles (1.37e7 area units) removed against roughly 96 added adders of about 22 bits (~2100 adder bits over all 42 module instances, on the order of 3e6 area units). The reduction trees keep the same depth for the block leaves in f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, and h3/h4 improve from depth 2 to depth 1 for their block leaf, so the period should not regress and the h3/h4 paths get shorter.

Per-module leaf arrival and tree shape (as in MAPPING). f1 has four leaves (blocks ×29, ×101, ×235 and soft ×15), reduced balanced at depth 2, exactly as revision 1's f1. f2/h2 have four leaves (blocks ×42, ×163 and soft ×4, ×255), depth 2. f3 and h1 have three leaves (two blocks, one soft), depth 2. h3/h4 have three leaves (one block ×109, soft ×9 and ×56), reduced as p + (t9 + t56) so the block product passes through a single adder.

Editor instructions.

  • Work from the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory; the kept candidate's edit is not present in it. Do not edit any other file and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma.
  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, replace only the dout <= ... product-sum statement inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) with the single statement given in MAPPING. Leave the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list, the register declarations and all COEF* defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though nothing reads it there, as in the original.
  • At module level declare wire [47:0] p0, p1, p2, p3; (only the ones that module uses; names free) and the soft wires listed in MAPPING with exactly the widths given, as continuous assigns. Do not narrow or widen them: the widths are chosen so no intermediate wraps.
  • Instantiate the blocks outside the always block, with named connections only: .A({11'b0, <tap>}), .D({11'b0, <tap>}), .B(18'd<c>), .PCIN(48'd0), .P(pN), .PCOUT(). The unpaired centre taps (f1 ×235) use .D(27'd0). Every input port is connected; PCIN is tied to the constant 0 on every block, permitted for a block that is not cascaded; no PCOUT is read.
  • Touch no other module.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned (WIDTH_5B = 16) and every coefficient is at most 255, so on each block A, D ≤ 65535, inside the 25 unsigned bits the block allows; the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and the sum reads as a positive signed value; B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The soft terms are the same identity followed by one shift-add, each sized to its exact range: t4 = 4·s0 ≤ 524280 < 2^19; t9 = 9·s0 ≤ 1179630 < 2^21; t12 = 12·s0 ≤ 1572840 < 2^21; t15 = 16·s − s with 16·s ≤ 2097120 < 2^21 and the difference non-negative; t56 = 64·s1 − 8·s1 with 64·s1 ≤ 8388480 < 2^23; t255 = 256·x3 − x3 with 256·x3 ≤ 16776960 < 2^24. No intermediate shift and no subtraction overflows or borrows, and every result is non-negative.
  • Module totals: f1 65535·525 = 34.4M, f2/h2 65535·673 = 44.1M, f3 65535·474, h1 65535·466, h3/h4 65535·348 — all below 2^28, so every leaf, every partial sum and the final sum fit in the 28-bit dout and far inside the blocks' 48 bits. In the original the sum is likewise assigned to the 28-bit dout, a truncation that can never fire. All wires are unsigned, so every addend is zero-extended to the 28-bit context of the dout assignment. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads, move inside a block. The pre-adder sums are not values of the original design. PCOUT drives nothing.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add and multiply) in parallel with combinational soft pair-adds and shift-adds → one or two levels of combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why.

  • Left because the folded pair's coefficient is a single shift-add, so a whole DSP tile (9.1 CLBs) would buy nothing and the soft term also reaches the reduction earlier than a block product does; their arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same sum: my_fir_f1.$mul$…1488$157 and …1490$161 (×15), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1542$169, …1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1716$210, …1722$221 (×4), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1545$174, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1719$215 (×255, an unpaired centre tap: one 24-bit subtract), my_fir_f3.$mul$…1602$184, …1607$193 (×12), my_fir_h1.$mul$…1661$197, …1666$206 (×15), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1775$225, …1780$234, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1833$238, …1838$247 (×9), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1776$226, …1779$232, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1834$239, …1837$245 (×56).
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for two reasons, neither a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding them (25 blocks per instance set, 150 blocks) would add roughly 88 DSP tiles, about +2.2e7 area units, while removing only a 20-bit adder tree worth a small fraction of that — the opposite of this pass's direction. (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 78 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in revision 1) is about 135 of the 306 DSP tiles, 56 fewer than revision 1's 191 — the compaction that should also shorten the 1.94 ns flop-to-A route.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output of sv_chip2_hierarchy_no_mem on every cycle after the testbench's reset phase (its first 8 cycles), on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (dsp48e2_preadd_ma.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

Delay chain, new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, else branch, ports, register declarations and all COEF* defines are untouched; no dsp48e2_preadd_ma module is defined in the design.

Every block is wired .A({11'b0,<tap>}), .D({11'b0,<tap>}), .B(18'd<c>), .PCIN(48'd0), .P(pN), .PCOUT() — all inputs connected, PCIN tied to constant 0 (no cascade), PCOUT read by nothing.

Soft: s2[16:0] = {1'b0,n_delay_reg2}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg4}, t15[20:0] = {s2,4'b0000}-{4'b0000,s2}. New statement: dout <= (p0[27:0] + p1[27:0]) + (p3[27:0] + t15);
  • my_fir_f2 (1542–1548): 2 blocks — u1 reg1/reg5 ×42, u2 reg2/reg4 ×163. Soft: s0[16:0], t4[18:0] = {s0,2'b00}, t255[23:0] = {n_delay_reg3,8'b0}-{8'b0,n_delay_reg3}. dout <= (p1[27:0] + p2[27:0]) + (t4 + t255);
  • my_fir_f3 (1602–1607): 2 blocks — u1 reg1/reg5 ×77, u2 reg2/reg4 ×148. Soft: s0, t12[20:0] = {1'b0,s0,3'b000}+{2'b00,s0,2'b00}. dout <= (p1[27:0] + p2[27:0]) + t12;
  • my_fir_h1 (1661–1666): 2 blocks — u1 reg1/reg5 ×25, u2 reg2/reg4 ×193. Soft: s0, t15[20:0]. dout <= (p1[27:0] + p2[27:0]) + t15;

The fltr_compute_* multiplies and every other module are unchanged. No ASSUMES: line is needed: taps are 16-bit unsigned, so A,D ≤ 65535 (inside the 25 unsigned bits), D+A ≤ 131070 < 2^26 keeps the 27-bit pre-adder sum positive-signed, B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit, and every module total (≤ 44.1M) fits in the 28-bit dout.

Beyond check.sh I ran an iverilog cross-check of the seven rewritten modules against golden models of the original coefficient sums, using the provided sim_reference/dsp48e2_preadd_ma.v, with all registers forced to 0 at time 0: 20000 cycles of random din/new_data_rdy and 4000 cycles of near-maximum din (0xFFFF/0xFFFE), comparing dout and output_data_ready each cycle — 0 errors in both runs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

// dsp48e2_preadd_ma: behavioural model of the arch mode dsp48e2_preadd_ma_mode, which mimics the AMD DSP48E2 slice
// as a pre-adder multiply on the P cascade: "C +/- ( B x ( D +/- A ) + W + CIN )" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2)
// with AMULTSEL = AD, PREADDINSEL = A, BMULTSEL = B, USE_MULT = MULTIPLY, INMODE = 00100 (D enabled,
// add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000,
// CARRYIN = 0, C unused, AREG = BREG = DREG = ADREG = MREG = 0 and PREG = 0. INMODE and OPMODE are fixed
// inside the mode. Reference for every per-cycle question: AMD's simulation model
// /tools/Xilinx/Vivado/2024.1/data/verilog/src/unisims/DSP48E2.v (Vivado 2024.1; registers start at 0 in the
// initial block at lines 1178-1217), read in place and never copied.
// P = PCIN + (D + A) * B: the pre-adder sum wraps at 27 bits and is read as signed, the product is
// signed 27x18, the sum wraps at 48 bits. No register: P and PCOUT are combinational from A, D, B and PCIN, and PCOUT = P.
// PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or 0.
// Signed two's complement throughout, as the real block; unsigned data must have a zero top bit on
// each operand. Every register starts at 0: AMD's simulation model starts its registers at 0 in the
// `initial` block(s) cited below (Vivado 2024.1). Resets are synchronous, active high, clear only the
// register(s) they name and win over that register's clock enable. Timing figures and tile area are
// this project's arch's own, not AMD's. One block per DSP tile.
module dsp48e2_preadd_ma (
    input [26:0] A,
    input [26:0] D,
    input [17:0] B,
    input [47:0] PCIN,
    output [47:0] P,
    output [47:0] PCOUT
);
    wire [26:0] ad = D + A;                                   // 27-bit pre-adder, wraps
    wire signed [44:0] m = $signed(ad) * $signed(B);          // signed 27x18 -> 45, exact
    wire [47:0] sum = PCIN + {{3{m[44]}}, m};               // modulo 2^48
    assign P = sum;
    assign PCOUT = sum;
endmodule

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.

PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate (revision 1). Revision 1 put every folded symmetric pair on a block: 132 blocks, measured 8.286 ns and 8.204e7 area, product 6.80e8. Its measured path shows where the time goes: 1.940 ns of wire from the tap flop to A, 2.140 ns of block, then 1.504 ns for the first 28-bit add (0.752 wire + 0.752 chain), 0.861 ns for the second, and 1.752 ns for the new_data_rdy enable mux at dout. Two facts follow. First, more than half the period (5.08 ns of 8.29) is routing wire, so shrinking the placement is the main remaining delay lever, and DSP tiles are what spread it: a block tile is 253779 area units, 9.1 CLBs. Second, a soft carry-chain level costs ~1.5 ns from its driver, so a folded product whose coefficient needs exactly one add/subtract of two shifted copies of the pair sum reaches the tree at ~2.9 ns — well before a block product's 4.18 ns — while costing two small adders instead of a whole tile.

This pass therefore keeps on the block exactly those folded products whose coefficient is expensive in soft logic (three or more non-zero CSD terms, i.e. two or more chained adders after the pair sum: 29, 101, 235, 42, 163, 77, 148, 25, 193, 109) and computes outside the block the folded products whose coefficient is a single shift-add (15, 12, 9, 56, 255, and the ×4 already left soft in revision 1). Those terms gain nothing from a 2.14 ns multiplier and a whole tile. The pre-adder folding itself, the per-module reduction depth and every register are unchanged from revision 1, so this is a strict area reduction with no structural risk: blocks fall from 132 to 78, i.e. 54 DSP tiles (1.37e7 area units) removed against roughly 96 added adders of about 22 bits (~2100 adder bits over all 42 module instances, on the order of 3e6 area units). The reduction trees keep the same depth for the block leaves in f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, and h3/h4 improve from depth 2 to depth 1 for their block leaf, so the period should not regress and the h3/h4 paths get shorter.

Per-module leaf arrival and tree shape (as in MAPPING). f1 has four leaves (blocks ×29, ×101, ×235 and soft ×15), reduced balanced at depth 2, exactly as revision 1's f1. f2/h2 have four leaves (blocks ×42, ×163 and soft ×4, ×255), depth 2. f3 and h1 have three leaves (two blocks, one soft), depth 2. h3/h4 have three leaves (one block ×109, soft ×9 and ×56), reduced as p + (t9 + t56) so the block product passes through a single adder.

  • Work from the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory; the kept candidate's edit is not present in it. Do not edit any other file and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma.
  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, replace only the dout <= ... product-sum statement inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) with the single statement given in MAPPING. Leave the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list, the register declarations and all COEF* defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though nothing reads it there, as in the original.
  • At module level declare wire [47:0] p0, p1, p2, p3; (only the ones that module uses; names free) and the soft wires listed in MAPPING with exactly the widths given, as continuous assigns. Do not narrow or widen them: the widths are chosen so no intermediate wraps.
  • Instantiate the blocks outside the always block, with named connections only: .A({11'b0, <tap>}), .D({11'b0, <tap>}), .B(18'd<c>), .PCIN(48'd0), .P(pN), .PCOUT(). The unpaired centre taps (f1 ×235) use .D(27'd0). Every input port is connected; PCIN is tied to the constant 0 on every block, permitted for a block that is not cascaded; no PCOUT is read.
  • Touch no other module.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned (WIDTH_5B = 16) and every coefficient is at most 255, so on each block A, D ≤ 65535, inside the 25 unsigned bits the block allows; the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and the sum reads as a positive signed value; B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The soft terms are the same identity followed by one shift-add, each sized to its exact range: t4 = 4·s0 ≤ 524280 < 2^19; t9 = 9·s0 ≤ 1179630 < 2^21; t12 = 12·s0 ≤ 1572840 < 2^21; t15 = 16·s − s with 16·s ≤ 2097120 < 2^21 and the difference non-negative; t56 = 64·s1 − 8·s1 with 64·s1 ≤ 8388480 < 2^23; t255 = 256·x3 − x3 with 256·x3 ≤ 16776960 < 2^24. No intermediate shift and no subtraction overflows or borrows, and every result is non-negative.
  • Module totals: f1 65535·525 = 34.4M, f2/h2 65535·673 = 44.1M, f3 65535·474, h1 65535·466, h3/h4 65535·348 — all below 2^28, so every leaf, every partial sum and the final sum fit in the 28-bit dout and far inside the blocks' 48 bits. In the original the sum is likewise assigned to the 28-bit dout, a truncation that can never fire. All wires are unsigned, so every addend is zero-extended to the 28-bit context of the dout assignment. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads, move inside a block. The pre-adder sums are not values of the original design. PCOUT drives nothing.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add and multiply) in parallel with combinational soft pair-adds and shift-adds → one or two levels of combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why.

  • Left because the folded pair's coefficient is a single shift-add, so a whole DSP tile (9.1 CLBs) would buy nothing and the soft term also reaches the reduction earlier than a block product does; their arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same sum: my_fir_f1.$mul$…1488$157 and …1490$161 (×15), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1542$169, …1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1716$210, …1722$221 (×4), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1545$174, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1719$215 (×255, an unpaired centre tap: one 24-bit subtract), my_fir_f3.$mul$…1602$184, …1607$193 (×12), my_fir_h1.$mul$…1661$197, …1666$206 (×15), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1775$225, …1780$234, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1833$238, …1838$247 (×9), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1776$226, …1779$232, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1834$239, …1837$245 (×56).
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for two reasons, neither a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding them (25 blocks per instance set, 150 blocks) would add roughly 88 DSP tiles, about +2.2e7 area units, while removing only a 20-bit adder tree worth a small fraction of that — the opposite of this pass's direction. (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 78 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in revision 1) is about 135 of the 306 DSP tiles, 56 fewer than revision 1's 191 — the compaction that should also shorten the 1.94 ns flop-to-A route.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would also become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family.

ACCEPT

Checked against the plan, the contract and the correctness rules.

Plan conformance

  • 13 instantiations, matching the plan's count and distribution (f1: u0,u1,u3 at stereovision2.v:1478/1486/1494; f2: 1561/1569; f3: 1640/1648; h1: 1718/1726; h2: 1793/1801; h3: 1872; h4: 1944). The log independently reports 13 instantiations in the DUT.
  • Every A/D/B pairing and every coefficient matches MAPPING exactly (29/101/235; 42/163; 77/148; 25/193; 42/163; 109; 109), with A,D = {11'b0, tap} and the unpaired f1 centre tap on .D(27'd0).
  • Soft wires and widths are exactly as specified: s0/s1/s2 17 b, t4 19 b, t9/t12/t15 21 b, t56 23 b, t255 24 b; each dout <= statement is the one given in MAPPING.
  • Nothing outside the seven my_fir_* modules changed (only trailing-whitespace on the blank line before output_data_ready); no dsp48e2_preadd_ma module definition was added; fltr_compute_* and the delay chains, guards, output_data_ready, else branch, ports and COEF* defines are untouched. n_delay_reg3 remains in the f3/h1/h3/h4 chains unread, as in the original.

Ports and outputs

  • All four inputs connected by name on every instance; PCIN = 48'd0 on all 13 (legal tie-off for a non-cascaded block); PCOUT left unconnected and read by nothing; P drives only the per-module dout reduction, as the plan says.

Correctness

  • Same behaviour / terms: folding is exact over the integers (a·c + b·c = (a+b)·c), and each soft term reproduces its coefficient ({s,4'b0}-{4'b0,s} = 15·s, {1'b0,s,3'b0}+{2'b0,s,2'b0} = 12·s, {1'b0,s,3'b0}+{4'b0,s} = 9·s, {s,6'b0}-{3'b0,s,3'b0} = 56·s, {x,8'b0}-{8'b0,x} = 255·x, {s,2'b0} = 4·s). Every term of each original sum is present; f3/h1/h3/h4 correctly omit the n_delay_reg3 term the original omits.
  • Widths: with WIDTH_5B=16, pair sums ≤ 131070, so t4≤524280<2^19, t9≤1179630 and t12≤1572840 and t15≤1966050<2^21, t56≤7339920<2^23, t255≤16711425<2^24 — no concat, shift or subtraction wraps, and every subtraction is non-negative. Module totals (max 65535·673 = 44.1 M) stay below 2^28, so the 28-bit dout context and the P[27:0] slices never truncate, matching the original's 32-bit-then-truncate behaviour bit for bit.
  • Block operand limits: A,D ≤ 65535 (≤25 unsigned bits), pre-adder sum ≤ 131070 < 2^26 so bit 26 is 0 and the sum reads positive signed; B ≤ 235 has a zero top bit. No wrap at 48 bits.
  • Visibility: the only values moved inside blocks are the tap products, which nothing else in the design reads; din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their registers and their readers outside. The pre-adder sums are new values, not original-design signals.
  • Registers and reset: no register added, moved or removed; the blocks are combinational and sit outside the always, so the new_data_rdy-enabled dout register keeps one stage and the same post-reset behaviour. Nothing depends on an unknown start-up value, so no ASSUMES: line is needed.

1	// dsp48e2_preadd_ma: behavioural model of the arch mode dsp48e2_preadd_ma_mode, which mimics the AMD DSP48E2 slice
2	// as a pre-adder multiply on the P cascade: "C +/- ( B x ( D +/- A ) + W + CIN )" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2)
3	// with AMULTSEL = AD, PREADDINSEL = A, BMULTSEL = B, USE_MULT = MULTIPLY, INMODE = 00100 (D enabled,
4	// add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000,
5	// CARRYIN = 0, C unused, AREG = BREG = DREG = ADREG = MREG = 0 and PREG = 0. INMODE and OPMODE are fixed
6	// inside the mode. Reference for every per-cycle question: AMD's simulation model
7	// /tools/Xilinx/Vivado/2024.1/data/verilog/src/unisims/DSP48E2.v (Vivado 2024.1; registers start at 0 in the
8	// initial block at lines 1178-1217), read in place and never copied.
9	// P = PCIN + (D + A) * B: the pre-adder sum wraps at 27 bits and is read as signed, the product is
10	// signed 27x18, the sum wraps at 48 bits. No register: P and PCOUT are combinational from A, D, B and PCIN, and PCOUT = P.
11	// PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or 0.
12	// Signed two's complement throughout, as the real block; unsigned data must have a zero top bit on
13	// each operand. Every register starts at 0: AMD's simulation model starts its registers at 0 in the
14	// `initial` block(s) cited below (Vivado 2024.1). Resets are synchronous, active high, clear only the
15	// register(s) they name and win over that register's clock enable. Timing figures and tile area are
16	// this project's arch's own, not AMD's. One block per DSP tile.
17	module dsp48e2_preadd_ma (
18	    input [26:0] A,
19	    input [26:0] D,
20	    input [17:0] B,
21	    input [47:0] PCIN,
22	    output [47:0] P,
23	    output [47:0] PCOUT
24	);
25	    wire [26:0] ad = D + A;                                   // 27-bit pre-adder, wraps
26	    wire signed [44:0] m = $signed(ad) * $signed(B);          // signed 27x18 -> 45, exact
27	    wire [47:0] sum = PCIN + {{3{m[44]}}, m};               // modulo 2^48
28	    assign P = sum;
29	    assign PCOUT = sum;
30	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The block on this architecture

These are read from the architecture file.

  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. The block has no reset: "same behavior" must hold after every reset of the design, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original on the testbench's stimulus, which does not respect it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Goal

Propose a correct rewrite onto the block. The loop measures it against the original design on area × delay; you are not asked to predict the result.

Output
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when you propose no rewrite>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

No rewrite
  • REGIONS: NONE: You propose no rewrite this time. The plan states why, from what you were given: no correct rewrite, or nothing left to try. The run then ends and keeps the best result so far if its median over every seed is below the original's, and the original design otherwise (also when no rewrite has beaten it).
What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left: a correctness reason, or "not chosen this pass"; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the REGIONS line; read the source first.
  • Your reply is read by the framework, not answered by a person, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.
Measured result of your plan

Every candidate tried so far in this run, in order. Each row gives the candidate's figures at seed 1, which every measured candidate was measured at, and then, where more seeds were run, the median over the seeds named, which is the figure the loop compared. The period is register to register (I/O pads not timed). The product is the run's objective, area × delay; the ratios are against the baseline's figures (the median of five seeds, 1 to 5; A/A0 area, D/D0 period, and their product). PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate (revision 1). Revision 1 put every folded symmetric pair on a block: 132 blocks, measured 8.286 ns and 8.204e7 area, product 6.80e8. Its measured path shows where the time goes: 1.940 ns of wire from the tap flop to A, 2.140 ns of block, then 1.504 ns for the first 28-bit add (0.752 wire + 0.752 chain), 0.861 ns for the second, and 1.752 ns for the new_data_rdy enable mux at dout. Two facts follow. First, more than half the period (5.08 ns of 8.29) is routing wire, so shrinking the placement is the main remaining delay lever, and DSP tiles are what spread it: a block tile is 253779 area units, 9.1 CLBs. Second, a soft carry-chain level costs ~1.5 ns from its driver, so a folded product whose coefficient needs exactly one add/subtract of two shifted copies of the pair sum reaches the tree at ~2.9 ns — well before a block product's 4.18 ns — while costing two small adders instead of a whole tile.

This pass therefore keeps on the block exactly those folded products whose coefficient is expensive in soft logic (three or more non-zero CSD terms, i.e. two or more chained adders after the pair sum: 29, 101, 235, 42, 163, 77, 148, 25, 193, 109) and computes outside the block the folded products whose coefficient is a single shift-add (15, 12, 9, 56, 255, and the ×4 already left soft in revision 1). Those terms gain nothing from a 2.14 ns multiplier and a whole tile. The pre-adder folding itself, the per-module reduction depth and every register are unchanged from revision 1, so this is a strict area reduction with no structural risk: blocks fall from 132 to 78, i.e. 54 DSP tiles (1.37e7 area units) removed against roughly 96 added adders of about 22 bits (~2100 adder bits over all 42 module instances, on the order of 3e6 area units). The reduction trees keep the same depth for the block leaves in f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, and h3/h4 improve from depth 2 to depth 1 for their block leaf, so the period should not regress and the h3/h4 paths get shorter.

Per-module leaf arrival and tree shape (as in MAPPING). f1 has four leaves (blocks ×29, ×101, ×235 and soft ×15), reduced balanced at depth 2, exactly as revision 1's f1. f2/h2 have four leaves (blocks ×42, ×163 and soft ×4, ×255), depth 2. f3 and h1 have three leaves (two blocks, one soft), depth 2. h3/h4 have three leaves (one block ×109, soft ×9 and ×56), reduced as p + (t9 + t56) so the block product passes through a single adder.

Editor instructions.

  • Work from the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory; the kept candidate's edit is not present in it. Do not edit any other file and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma.
  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, replace only the dout <= ... product-sum statement inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) with the single statement given in MAPPING. Leave the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list, the register declarations and all COEF* defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though nothing reads it there, as in the original.
  • At module level declare wire [47:0] p0, p1, p2, p3; (only the ones that module uses; names free) and the soft wires listed in MAPPING with exactly the widths given, as continuous assigns. Do not narrow or widen them: the widths are chosen so no intermediate wraps.
  • Instantiate the blocks outside the always block, with named connections only: .A({11'b0, <tap>}), .D({11'b0, <tap>}), .B(18'd<c>), .PCIN(48'd0), .P(pN), .PCOUT(). The unpaired centre taps (f1 ×235) use .D(27'd0). Every input port is connected; PCIN is tied to the constant 0 on every block, permitted for a block that is not cascaded; no PCOUT is read.
  • Touch no other module.

Why this is exact.

  • Every tap is 16-bit unsigned (WIDTH_5B = 16) and every coefficient is at most 255, so on each block A, D ≤ 65535, inside the 25 unsigned bits the block allows; the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and the sum reads as a positive signed value; B ≤ 255 has a zero top bit. Folding a symmetric pair is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c.
  • The soft terms are the same identity followed by one shift-add, each sized to its exact range: t4 = 4·s0 ≤ 524280 < 2^19; t9 = 9·s0 ≤ 1179630 < 2^21; t12 = 12·s0 ≤ 1572840 < 2^21; t15 = 16·s − s with 16·s ≤ 2097120 < 2^21 and the difference non-negative; t56 = 64·s1 − 8·s1 with 64·s1 ≤ 8388480 < 2^23; t255 = 256·x3 − x3 with 256·x3 ≤ 16776960 < 2^24. No intermediate shift and no subtraction overflows or borrows, and every result is non-negative.
  • Module totals: f1 65535·525 = 34.4M, f2/h2 65535·673 = 44.1M, f3 65535·474, h1 65535·466, h3/h4 65535·348 — all below 2^28, so every leaf, every partial sum and the final sum fit in the 28-bit dout and far inside the blocks' 48 bits. In the original the sum is likewise assigned to the 28-bit dout, a truncation that can never fire. All wires are unsigned, so every addend is zero-extended to the 28-bit context of the dout assignment. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads, move inside a block. The pre-adder sums are not values of the original design. PCOUT drives nothing.
  • The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma blocks (pre-add and multiply) in parallel with combinational soft pair-adds and shift-adds → one or two levels of combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any converted module.

Candidates left, and why.

  • Left because the folded pair's coefficient is a single shift-add, so a whole DSP tile (9.1 CLBs) would buy nothing and the soft term also reaches the reduction earlier than a block product does; their arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same sum: my_fir_f1.$mul$…1488$157 and …1490$161 (×15), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1542$169, …1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1716$210, …1722$221 (×4), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1545$174, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1719$215 (×255, an unpaired centre tap: one 24-bit subtract), my_fir_f3.$mul$…1602$184, …1607$193 (×12), my_fir_h1.$mul$…1661$197, …1666$206 (×15), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1775$225, …1780$234, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1833$238, …1838$247 (×9), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1776$226, …1779$232, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1834$239, …1837$245 (×56).
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for two reasons, neither a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding them (25 blocks per instance set, 150 blocks) would add roughly 88 DSP tiles, about +2.2e7 area units, while removing only a 20-bit adder tree worth a small fraction of that — the opposite of this pass's direction. (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 78 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in revision 1) is about 135 of the 306 DSP tiles, 56 fewer than revision 1's 191 — the compaction that should also shorten the 1.94 ns flop-to-A route.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would also become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output of sv_chip2_hierarchy_no_mem on every cycle after the testbench's reset phase (its first 8 cycles). A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (dsp48e2_preadd_ma.v) are in sim_reference/.

Read these files in this directory: stereovision2.v

response

I'll read the source before planning.

REGIONS: my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1777$228, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1778$230, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1835$241, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1836$243
SHARED_REDUCTION: the dout register of my_fir_h3 and of my_fir_h4 (one reduction per module: dout <= p2[27:0] + (a9 + a56); no PCOUT→PCIN cascade)
BLOCKS: 12 (2 instantiations written in the source — one in my_fir_h3, one in my_fir_h4 — each module having 6 instances)
MAPPING: in both blocks A = {11'b0, n_delay_reg2} (16-bit unsigned tap zero-extended to 27), D = {11'b0, n_delay_reg4}, B = 18'd109, PCIN = 48'd0, P = p2 (the folded pair product, read as p2[27:0]), PCOUT left unconnected and read by nothing.

PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate (revision 2), and why. Revision 2's own measurement is the evidence for this pass. Going from revision 1 (132 blocks) to revision 2 (78 blocks) removed 54 DSP tiles (54 × 253779 = 1.370e7 area units) and the total area fell by only 9.32e6, so the soft shift-add logic that replaced those 54 folded products cost 4.38e6, i.e. ~81k per product for ~38 added adder bits each — about 2100 area units per adder bit. At that rate one DSP tile equals ~121 adder bits, while a folded constant product in soft logic costs at most 85 adder bits (17-bit pair sum + three shift-adds of 20-25 bits, for a coefficient with four non-zero CSD digits) ≈ 179k. Every coefficient in the my_fir_* family is therefore cheaper in soft logic than on a whole tile, by 73k (the worst 4-digit coefficients, 101/163/77/109) to 126k (the 3-digit ones, 29/42/25) per product. Revision 2 also got faster while shedding tiles, which matches the measured path: of its 8.00 ns, 5.19 ns is routing wire (1.627 ns flop→D, 0.96 + 0.79 ns between adders, 1.807 ns into the final LUT), and the DSP columns are what spread the placement.

Delay is not given up by this. On revision 2's own numbers a soft adder level costs ~1.05-1.15 ns from its driver and the first level from a flop ends at ~1.6-1.7 ns, so a leaf needing a pair sum plus two chained shift-adds lands at ~3.8 ns — the same place a block's P lands (0.103 + 1.627 + 2.140 = 3.87 ns), and a leaf needing one or two adds lands earlier. The reduction tree depth per module is unchanged (my_fir_h1 even improves from 5 levels to 4 by re-balancing its terms), so the register-to-register depth is the same or shorter, with 66 fewer DSP tiles to route around.

This pass therefore keeps the block only where it is provably off the critical path — the ×109 folded pair of my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4, the shallowest modules (3 leaves, block product passing through exactly one adder before dout, total 4 levels against the 5 of f1/f2/f3/h2) — and computes every other folded product as an exact CSD shift-add outside the block. 78 blocks → 12 blocks: 66 DSP tiles (1.675e7) removed against ~4750 added adder bits (~1.0e7), a net ~6.8e6 (≈9%) of area, with the delay expected flat or better.

  • In each my_fir_* module, change only two things: (a) add the module-level wire declarations, assigns and (in h3/h4) the block instantiation shown below, placed after the n_delay_reg6 declaration and before the always block; (b) replace the dout <= (din * COEF…) + …; statement inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) with the single dout <= …; line shown. Leave the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list, the register declarations and all `` COEF`` defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though nothing reads it there, as in the original.
  • Use exactly the wire widths and concatenation widths given: every operand of every +/- is written out to the full declared width, so no intermediate can wrap and no subtraction can borrow. Do not "simplify" a concatenation or narrow a wire. Wire names are free; u2 may be renamed.

Why this is exact.

  • The blocks. Every tap is 16-bit unsigned ( `WIDTH_5B = 16), so on each block A, D ≤ 65535, inside the 25 unsigned bits the block allows; the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and it reads as a positive signed value; B = 109 < 2^17 has a zero top bit. P = 109·(x2+x4) ≤ 14,286,630, far inside 48 bits, so p2[27:0] is the exact product. Folding is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c, and 109 is COEF2_3/COEF4_3 and COEF2_4/COEF4_4 alike (lines 1736/1738, 1794/1796).
  • The soft terms. Each is the same folding identity followed by CSD shift-adds: 29 = 32−4+1, 101 = 128−32+4+1, 15 = 16−1, 235 = (256−16)−(4+1), 4, 42 = (32+8)+2, 163 = (128+32)+(2+1), 255 = 256−1, 12 = 8+4, 77 = (64+8)+(4+1), 148 = (128+16)+4, 15/24/192 with the leftover s1+s2 giving 25 and 193, 9 = 8+1, 56 = 64−8. With every pair sum ≤ 131070 and every centre tap ≤ 65535: 28·s0 ≤ 3,669,960 < 2^22 and 29·s0 ≤ 3,801,030 < 2^22; 96·s1 ≤ 12,582,720 and 101·s1 ≤ 13,238,070 < 2^24; 5·s1 ≤ 655,350 < 2^20; 15·s ≤ 1,966,050 < 2^21; 240·x3 ≤ 15,728,400 and 235·x3 ≤ 15,400,725 < 2^24; 5·x3 ≤ 327,675 < 2^19; 4·s0 ≤ 524,280 < 2^19; 40·s1 ≤ 5,242,800 and 42·s1 ≤ 5,504,940 < 2^23; 160·s2 ≤ 20,971,200 and 163·s2 ≤ 21,364,410 < 2^25; 3·s2 ≤ 393,210 < 2^19; 255·x3 ≤ 16,711,425 < 2^24; 12·s0 ≤ 1,572,840 < 2^21; 72·s1 ≤ 9,437,040 and 77·s1 ≤ 10,092,390 < 2^24; 144·s2 ≤ 18,874,080 and 148·s2 ≤ 19,398,360 < 2^25; 24·s1 ≤ 3,145,680 < 2^22; 192·s2 ≤ 25,165,440 < 2^25; s1+s2 ≤ 262,140 < 2^18; 9·s0 ≤ 1,179,630 < 2^21; 56·s1 ≤ 7,339,920 < 2^23. Every subtraction has a minuend at least as large as its subtrahend (32s ≥ 4s, 16s ≥ s, 240x ≥ 5x, 256x ≥ x, 64s ≥ 8s), so no intermediate is negative and none wraps.
  • Module totals. f1 65535·525 = 34,405,875; f2/h2 65535·673 = 44,105,055; f3 65535·474 = 31,063,590; h1 65535·466 = 30,539,310; h3/h4 65535·348 = 22,806,180 — all below 2^28, so every partial sum and the final sum fit the 28-bit dout, exactly as in the original, where the same sum is assigned to the same 28-bit register (a truncation that can never fire). All wires are unsigned, so in the 28-bit context of the dout assignment every addend is zero-extended. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility. The taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the two ×109 products, which nothing else in the design reads, move inside a block. The pre-adder sums are not values of the original design. PCOUT drives nothing, and PCIN is the constant 0 on both blocks, permitted for a block that is not cascaded.
  • Registers and reset. The block has no register and the rewrite adds none, so nothing depends on an unknown start-up value and behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region (my_fir_h3.…1777$228/…1778$230 and my_fir_h4.…1835$241/…1836$243): before — n_delay_reg2 / n_delay_reg4 → combinational constant multiply by 109 → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same two registers → combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma (pre-add then multiply) → one combinational 28-bit add with the soft terms → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. No register is added, moved or removed in any module.

Candidates left, and why.

  • Left because a whole DSP tile (253779 area units, 9.1 CLBs) costs more than the exact soft shift-add that replaces it (73k-126k less per product on revision 2's measured area-per-adder-bit), while reaching the reduction tree no later than a block's P does; the arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same sum — all remaining my_fir_* products: my_fir_f1 lines 1486$154, 1487$155, 1488$157, 1489$159, 1490$161, 1491$163, 1492$165; my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1543$170, 1544$172, 1545$174, 1546$176, 1547$178, 1548$180; my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1603$185, 1604$187, 1605$189, 1606$191, 1607$193; my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1662$198, 1663$200, 1664$202, 1665$204, 1666$206; my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1717$211, 1718$213, 1719$215, 1720$217, 1721$219, 1722$221; my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1776$226, 1779$232, 1780$234; my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1834$239, 1837$245, 1838$247.
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for two reasons, neither a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × ≤9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding them would add roughly 88 DSP tiles (+2.2e7) while removing only a 20-bit adder tree worth a small fraction of that — the opposite of this pass's direction. (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product reaching 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for the coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 12 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, ~60 as packed in revision 2) is about 72 of the 306 DSP tiles, 66 fewer than revision 2's 138 — the compaction that should also shorten the 1.6-1.8 ns routes that make up two thirds of revision 2's period.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family. Separately, the my_fir_* coefficients are so small (≤ 255, taps 16-bit unsigned) that a DSP of any kind is larger and no faster than CSD shift-adds here; a design that needed the block's strength would have to widen the coefficients past ~12 bits.
