#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

Task

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The block on this architecture

  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.
The design

The file stereovision2.v is the edited design. The edit is the diff below, taken against the original source.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. The block has no reset: "same behavior" must hold after every reset of the design, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original on the testbench's stimulus, which does not respect it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.

In every block A and D carry a 16-bit unsigned tap zero-extended to 27 bits ({11'b0, tap}), B carries that folded pair's coefficient as 18'd<c> (top bit 0), PCIN is 48'd0 (not cascaded), P is read as P[27:0], PCOUT is left unconnected and read by nothing. PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate (revision 2), and why. Revision 2 measured 8.003 ns with 78 blocks. Its reported path is: flop 0.103 → 1.627 ns of wire → block 2.140 → add 1.070 → add 1.110 → new_data_rdy enable mux 1.960. Two numbers decide this pass. (1) A block leaf becomes available 3.87 ns after the clock edge, and every block product must still pass through at least one soft adder (1.05 ns) and the enable mux (1.96 ns): the floor for a module with one block is ≈ 6.9 ns, and a module with two block products pays an extra adder level to merge them, pinning it at ≈ 7.9-8.0 ns. That is exactly where revision 2 sits. (2) Counting constant multiplies by CSD tree depth rather than by number of adds, every coefficient in these filters is at most two adder levels past the folded pair sum: 101={64,32,4,1}, 163={128,32,2,1}, 235={256,−16,−4,−1}, 77={64,8,4,1}, 109={128,−16,−2,−1} are 4 terms = 2 levels; 29={32,−2,−1}, 42={32,8,2}, 148={128,16,4}, 193={128,64,1}, 25={16,8,1} are 3 terms = 2 levels; 15, 12, 9, 56, 255 are 1 level; 4 is a wire. So a folded soft product lands at ≈ 0.1 + 3×1.0 = 3.2 ns, i.e. earlier than a block product, and a whole module's soft remainder lands at 4 levels ≈ 3.9-4.7 ns, i.e. about the same time as a block product.

Therefore this pass goes to exactly one block per my_fir_* module, carrying the most expensive coefficient (the one with the most CSD terms, which also removes the most soft adders), with every other tap product computed in soft shift-add logic and merged into a single soft value that meets the block product at the final adder. Each module then has the shape dout <= P + soft: one adder level after the block instead of two. Blocks fall from 78 to 42 (−36 DSP tiles, −9.1e6 area units) against roughly 108 added adders of about 22 bits over all 42 module instances (on the order of +4e6), so area should fall by about 7% while the my_fir critical path loses one adder level (≈ −1.0 ns) if the soft trees meet the block, and is unchanged in the worst case. Downside is bounded: if soft levels turn out to cost ~1.3 ns the period returns to about today's and the loop keeps revision 2.

Leave the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list, the register declarations and all COEF* defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though nothing reads it there, as in the original.
  • Declare the wires at module level with exactly the widths given (they are chosen so that no intermediate value wraps and no assignment truncates; the LHS width sets the self-determined context of each expression, so do not narrow them), write the assigns as continuous assignments outside the always block, and instantiate the block outside the always block with named connections only. Every input port is connected; PCIN is tied to the constant 48'd0 on every block, which is permitted for a block that is not cascaded; no PCOUT is read.

Per module (x0 = din, x1..x6 = n_delay_reg1..6):

my_fir_f1 (29,101,15,235,15,101,29) — block ×101 on (x1,x5):

wire [47:0] p101; wire [16:0] s0, s2; wire [18:0] a3, g5;
wire [21:0] t29;  wire [20:0] t15;    wire [23:0] g240, t235;

dout <= p101[27:0] + soft;

Why this is exact.

  • Folding is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c, and each module's coefficient set is symmetric (f1 29/29, 101/101, 15/15; f2 and h2 4/4, 42/42, 163/163; f3 12/12, 77/77, 148/148; h1 15/15, 25/25, 193/193; h3 and h4 9/9, 56/56, 109/109), with the centre tap handled separately (235·x3 in f1, 255·x3 in f2/h2; f3, h1, h3, h4 have coefficient 0 there and the original statement omits n_delay_reg3 — my rewrite omits it too).
  • Block operand limits: every tap is 16-bit unsigned (WIDTH_5B = 16), so A, D ≤ 65535, within the 25 unsigned bits allowed; the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and the sum reads as a positive signed value; each B (101, 163, 77, 193, 109) is ≤ 255 with a zero top bit. PCIN = 0, so P = (D+A)*B exactly, far inside 48 bits (largest 193·131070 = 25,296,510).
  • Soft terms, each sized to its exact range, all operands unsigned and all results non-negative, so no shift, subtraction or assignment wraps: 3·s0 ≤ 393,210 < 2^19; 29·s0 ≤ 3,801,030 < 2^22 (and 32·s0 ≤ 4,194,240 < 2^22); 15·s2 ≤ 1,966,050 < 2^21; 240·x3 ≤ 15,728,400 < 2^24; 5·x3 ≤ 327,675 < 2^19; 235·x3 ≤ 15,400,725 < 2^24; 4·s0 ≤ 524,280 < 2^19; 40·s1 ≤ 5,242,800 and 42·s1 ≤ 5,504,940 < 2^23; 255·x3 ≤ 16,711,425 < 2^24; 12·s0 ≤ 1,572,840 < 2^21; 144·s2 ≤ 18,874,080 and 148·s2 ≤ 19,398,360 < 2^25; 24·s1 ≤ 3,145,680 and 25·s1 ≤ 3,276,750 < 2^22; 9·s0 ≤ 1,179,630 < 2^21; 64·s1 ≤ 8,388,480 and 56·s1 ≤ 7,339,920 < 2^23. Every subtraction (32s0−3s0, 16s2−s2, 256x3−16x3, 240x3−5x3, 256x3−x3, 16s0−s0, 64s1−8s1) has a non-negative result, so no borrow leaves the declared width.
  • Partial sums and totals: f1 w ≤ 17,366,775 and soft ≤ 21,167,805 (< 2^25); f2/h2 v ≤ 17,235,705 and soft ≤ 22,740,645; f3 soft ≤ 20,971,200; h1 soft ≤ 5,242,800; h3/h4 soft ≤ 8,519,550. Module totals: f1 65535·525 = 34,405,875; f2/h2 65535·673 = 44,105,055; f3 65535·474 = 31,063,590; h1 65535·466 = 30,539,310; h3/h4 65535·348 = 22,806,180 — all below 2^28, so the 28-bit dout assignment truncates nothing, exactly as in the original (which also assigns this sum to the 28-bit dout). All wires are unsigned, so every addend is zero-extended into the 28-bit context of the dout assignment. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads (dout is the only other value, and it is unchanged), move inside a block or into the soft terms. The pre-adder sums and all t*/g*/soft wires are new internal values that nothing else reads. PCOUT drives nothing, as required for a block whose output must stay on general routing.
  • Registers and reset: the block has no register and the rewrite adds none — every new wire is combinational. No register is added, moved or removed, so behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged and nothing depends on an unknown start-up value.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → one combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma (pre-add and multiply) in parallel with the combinational soft pair-adds and shift-add tree → one final combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. Unchanged in every converted module.

Per-module leaf arrival and tree shape. Soft values ready one adder level after the taps (the pair sums s0, s1, s2 and the x3 partials) are reduced by a balanced tree so that soft is ready in 3 further levels for f1 (7 level-1 values), f2/h2 (5), f3 (5), h1 (5), and in 2 further levels for h3/h4 (4). The block product (≈3.87 ns measured) then meets soft at a single final adder, so the block passes through exactly one adder level in every module — against two levels in revision 2 for f1, f2, f3, h1, h2.

Candidates left, and why.

  • Left because the folded pair's (or centre tap's) coefficient is cheap in soft logic — at most two adder levels past the pair sum, so it reaches the reduction no later than a block product would, while a block would cost a whole DSP tile (9.1 CLBs). Their arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same dout sum: my_fir_f1.$mul$…1486$154, …1492$165 (×29), …1488$157, …1490$161 (×15), …1489$159 (×235); my_fir_f2.$mul$…1542$169, …1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1716$210, …1722$221 (×4), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1543$170, …1547$178, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1717$211, …1721$219 (×42), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1545$174, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1719$215 (×255); my_fir_f3.$mul$…1602$184, …1607$193 (×12), …1604$187, …1605$189 (×148); my_fir_h1.$mul$…1661$197, …1666$206 (×15), …1662$198, …1665$204 (×25); my_fir_h3.$mul$…1775$225, …1780$234, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1833$238, …1838$247 (×9), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1776$226, …1779$232, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1834$239, …1837$245 (×56).
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for two reasons, neither a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding their symmetric pairs would need about 4 blocks per module instance, 150+ tiles where 62 are used now — the opposite of this pass's direction — and moving them to soft logic instead costs more CLB area than the 62 tiles it frees (≈12 shift-adders per instance over 42 instances). (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 42 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in revision 1) is about 99 of the 306 DSP tiles, 39 fewer than revision 2's 138 — a compaction that should also shorten the 1.63 ns flop-to-A route and the 1.81 ns route into the enable mux.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family.

1	// dsp48e2_preadd_ma: behavioural model of the arch mode dsp48e2_preadd_ma_mode, which mimics the AMD DSP48E2 slice
2	// as a pre-adder multiply on the P cascade: "C +/- ( B x ( D +/- A ) + W + CIN )" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2)
3	// with AMULTSEL = AD, PREADDINSEL = A, BMULTSEL = B, USE_MULT = MULTIPLY, INMODE = 00100 (D enabled,
4	// add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000,
5	// CARRYIN = 0, C unused, AREG = BREG = DREG = ADREG = MREG = 0 and PREG = 0. INMODE and OPMODE are fixed
6	// inside the mode. Reference for every per-cycle question: AMD's simulation model
7	// /tools/Xilinx/Vivado/2024.1/data/verilog/src/unisims/DSP48E2.v (Vivado 2024.1; registers start at 0 in the
8	// initial block at lines 1178-1217), read in place and never copied.
9	// P = PCIN + (D + A) * B: the pre-adder sum wraps at 27 bits and is read as signed, the product is
10	// signed 27x18, the sum wraps at 48 bits. No register: P and PCOUT are combinational from A, D, B and PCIN, and PCOUT = P.
11	// PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or 0.
12	// Signed two's complement throughout, as the real block; unsigned data must have a zero top bit on
13	// each operand. Every register starts at 0: AMD's simulation model starts its registers at 0 in the
14	// `initial` block(s) cited below (Vivado 2024.1). Resets are synchronous, active high, clear only the
15	// register(s) they name and win over that register's clock enable. Timing figures and tile area are
16	// this project's arch's own, not AMD's. One block per DSP tile.
17	module dsp48e2_preadd_ma (
18	    input [26:0] A,
19	    input [26:0] D,
20	    input [17:0] B,
21	    input [47:0] PCIN,
22	    output [47:0] P,
23	    output [47:0] PCOUT
24	);
25	    wire [26:0] ad = D + A;                                   // 27-bit pre-adder, wraps
26	    wire signed [44:0] m = $signed(ad) * $signed(B);          // signed 27x18 -> 45, exact
27	    wire [47:0] sum = PCIN + {{3{m[44]}}, m};               // modulo 2^48
28	    assign P = sum;
29	    assign PCOUT = sum;
30	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The block on this architecture

These are read from the architecture file.

  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. The block has no reset: "same behavior" must hold after every reset of the design, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original on the testbench's stimulus, which does not respect it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Goal

Propose a correct rewrite onto the block. The loop measures it against the original design on area × delay; you are not asked to predict the result.

PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate (revision 2), and why. Revision 2 measured 8.003 ns with 78 blocks. Its reported path is: flop 0.103 → 1.627 ns of wire → block 2.140 → add 1.070 → add 1.110 → new_data_rdy enable mux 1.960. Two numbers decide this pass. (1) A block leaf becomes available 3.87 ns after the clock edge, and every block product must still pass through at least one soft adder (1.05 ns) and the enable mux (1.96 ns): the floor for a module with one block is ≈ 6.9 ns, and a module with two block products pays an extra adder level to merge them, pinning it at ≈ 7.9-8.0 ns. That is exactly where revision 2 sits. (2) Counting constant multiplies by CSD tree depth rather than by number of adds, every coefficient in these filters is at most two adder levels past the folded pair sum: 101={64,32,4,1}, 163={128,32,2,1}, 235={256,−16,−4,−1}, 77={64,8,4,1}, 109={128,−16,−2,−1} are 4 terms = 2 levels; 29={32,−2,−1}, 42={32,8,2}, 148={128,16,4}, 193={128,64,1}, 25={16,8,1} are 3 terms = 2 levels; 15, 12, 9, 56, 255 are 1 level; 4 is a wire. So a folded soft product lands at ≈ 0.1 + 3×1.0 = 3.2 ns, i.e. earlier than a block product, and a whole module's soft remainder lands at 4 levels ≈ 3.9-4.7 ns, i.e. about the same time as a block product.

Therefore this pass goes to exactly one block per my_fir_* module, carrying the most expensive coefficient (the one with the most CSD terms, which also removes the most soft adders), with every other tap product computed in soft shift-add logic and merged into a single soft value that meets the block product at the final adder. Each module then has the shape dout <= P + soft: one adder level after the block instead of two. Blocks fall from 78 to 42 (−36 DSP tiles, −9.1e6 area units) against roughly 108 added adders of about 22 bits over all 42 module instances (on the order of +4e6), so area should fall by about 7% while the my_fir critical path loses one adder level (≈ −1.0 ns) if the soft trees meet the block, and is unchanged in the worst case. Downside is bounded: if soft levels turn out to cost ~1.3 ns the period returns to about today's and the loop keeps revision 2.

assign s0   = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};
assign s2   = {1'b0, n_delay_reg2} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg4};
assign a3   = {s0, 1'b0} + s0;                 // 3*s0
assign t29  = {s0, 5'b00000} - a3;             // 29*s0
assign t15  = {s2, 4'b0000} - s2;              // 15*s2
assign g240 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b00000000} - {n_delay_reg3, 4'b0000};
assign g5   = {n_delay_reg3, 2'b00} + n_delay_reg3;
assign t235 = g240 - g5;                       // 235*x3
assign w    = t15 + t235;
assign soft = t29 + w;
dout <= p101[27:0] + soft;

my_fir_f2 (4,42,163,255,163,42,4) — block ×163 on (x2,x4):

wire [47:0] p163; wire [16:0] s0, s1; wire [18:0] t4;
wire [22:0] g40, t42; wire [23:0] t255; wire [24:0] v; wire [25:0] soft;

assign soft = t42 + v;
dout <= p163[27:0] + soft;

my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0,109,56,9) — block ×109 on (x2,x4):

wire [47:0] p109; wire [16:0] s0, s1; wire [20:0] t9;
wire [22:0] t56;  wire [23:0] soft;

assign soft = t9 + t56;
dout <= p109[27:0] + soft;

Why this is exact.

  • Folding is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c, and each module's coefficient set is symmetric (f1 29/29, 101/101, 15/15; f2 and h2 4/4, 42/42, 163/163; f3 12/12, 77/77, 148/148; h1 15/15, 25/25, 193/193; h3 and h4 9/9, 56/56, 109/109), with the centre tap handled separately (235·x3 in f1, 255·x3 in f2/h2; f3, h1, h3, h4 have coefficient 0 there and the original statement omits n_delay_reg3 — my rewrite omits it too).
  • Block operand limits: every tap is 16-bit unsigned (WIDTH_5B = 16), so A, D ≤ 65535, within the 25 unsigned bits allowed; the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and the sum reads as a positive signed value; each B (101, 163, 77, 193, 109) is ≤ 255 with a zero top bit. PCIN = 0, so P = (D+A)*B exactly, far inside 48 bits (largest 193·131070 = 25,296,510).
  • Soft terms, each sized to its exact range, all operands unsigned and all results non-negative, so no shift, subtraction or assignment wraps: 3·s0 ≤ 393,210 < 2^19; 29·s0 ≤ 3,801,030 < 2^22 (and 32·s0 ≤ 4,194,240 < 2^22); 15·s2 ≤ 1,966,050 < 2^21; 240·x3 ≤ 15,728,400 < 2^24; 5·x3 ≤ 327,675 < 2^19; 235·x3 ≤ 15,400,725 < 2^24; 4·s0 ≤ 524,280 < 2^19; 40·s1 ≤ 5,242,800 and 42·s1 ≤ 5,504,940 < 2^23; 255·x3 ≤ 16,711,425 < 2^24; 12·s0 ≤ 1,572,840 < 2^21; 144·s2 ≤ 18,874,080 and 148·s2 ≤ 19,398,360 < 2^25; 24·s1 ≤ 3,145,680 and 25·s1 ≤ 3,276,750 < 2^22; 9·s0 ≤ 1,179,630 < 2^21; 64·s1 ≤ 8,388,480 and 56·s1 ≤ 7,339,920 < 2^23. Every subtraction (32s0−3s0, 16s2−s2, 256x3−16x3, 240x3−5x3, 256x3−x3, 16s0−s0, 64s1−8s1) has a non-negative result, so no borrow leaves the declared width.
  • Partial sums and totals: f1 w ≤ 17,366,775 and soft ≤ 21,167,805 (< 2^25); f2/h2 v ≤ 17,235,705 and soft ≤ 22,740,645; f3 soft ≤ 20,971,200; h1 soft ≤ 5,242,800; h3/h4 soft ≤ 8,519,550. Module totals: f1 65535·525 = 34,405,875; f2/h2 65535·673 = 44,105,055; f3 65535·474 = 31,063,590; h1 65535·466 = 30,539,310; h3/h4 65535·348 = 22,806,180 — all below 2^28, so the 28-bit dout assignment truncates nothing, exactly as in the original (which also assigns this sum to the 28-bit dout). All wires are unsigned, so every addend is zero-extended into the 28-bit context of the dout assignment. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads (dout is the only other value, and it is unchanged), move inside a block or into the soft terms. The pre-adder sums and all t*/g*/soft wires are new internal values that nothing else reads. PCOUT drives nothing, as required for a block whose output must stay on general routing.
  • Registers and reset: the block has no register and the rewrite adds none — every new wire is combinational. No register is added, moved or removed, so behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged and nothing depends on an unknown start-up value.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → one combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma (pre-add and multiply) in parallel with the combinational soft pair-adds and shift-add tree → one final combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. Unchanged in every converted module.

Per-module leaf arrival and tree shape. Soft values ready one adder level after the taps (the pair sums s0, s1, s2 and the x3 partials) are reduced by a balanced tree so that soft is ready in 3 further levels for f1 (7 level-1 values), f2/h2 (5), f3 (5), h1 (5), and in 2 further levels for h3/h4 (4). The block product (≈3.87 ns measured) then meets soft at a single final adder, so the block passes through exactly one adder level in every module — against two levels in revision 2 for f1, f2, f3, h1, h2.

Candidates left, and why.

  • Left because the folded pair's (or centre tap's) coefficient is cheap in soft logic — at most two adder levels past the pair sum, so it reaches the reduction no later than a block product would, while a block would cost a whole DSP tile (9.1 CLBs). Their arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same dout sum: my_fir_f1.$mul$…1486$154, …1492$165 (×29), …1488$157, …1490$161 (×15), …1489$159 (×235); my_fir_f2.$mul$…1542$169, …1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1716$210, …1722$221 (×4), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1543$170, …1547$178, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1717$211, …1721$219 (×42), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1545$174, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1719$215 (×255); my_fir_f3.$mul$…1602$184, …1607$193 (×12), …1604$187, …1605$189 (×148); my_fir_h1.$mul$…1661$197, …1666$206 (×15), …1662$198, …1665$204 (×25); my_fir_h3.$mul$…1775$225, …1780$234, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1833$238, …1838$247 (×9), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1776$226, …1779$232, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1834$239, …1837$245 (×56).
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for two reasons, neither a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding their symmetric pairs would need about 4 blocks per module instance, 150+ tiles where 62 are used now — the opposite of this pass's direction — and moving them to soft logic instead costs more CLB area than the 62 tiles it frees (≈12 shift-adders per instance over 42 instances). (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 42 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in revision 1) is about 99 of the 306 DSP tiles, 39 fewer than revision 2's 138 — a compaction that should also shorten the 1.63 ns flop-to-A route and the 1.81 ns route into the enable mux.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output of sv_chip2_hierarchy_no_mem on every cycle after the testbench's reset phase (its first 8 cycles). A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (dsp48e2_preadd_ma.v) are in sim_reference/.

PLAN:

What this pass changes, and why. The kept candidate's own timing report settles where the period now comes from. Its worst path is six chained adders from a latch to a plain flip-flop with no clock-enable multiplexer at the end (lo14351.Q → $add~1795 … $add~1800 → $dff~1816^Q~18, 6.8997 ns). The only six-deep adder chain in this design that ends at an unguarded register is d_out_tmp <= q1+q2+q3+q4+q5+q6+q7 in the seven fltr_compute_* modules (lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073): seven sign-extended 20-bit terms, left-associative, six ripple adds, ~1.13 ns per level, and d_out_tmp has no enable. Every my_fir_* path, by contrast, must end in the new_data_rdy enable mux, which the earlier revision-2 report shows explicitly (1.960 ns); revision 2's my_fir path was 0.103 + 1.627 (route to A) + 2.140 (block) + 1.070 + 1.110 + 1.960 = 8.01 ns, and removing one adder level gave revision 4's my_fir shape at about 6.7 ns — at or just under the measured worst. So the my_fir_* block rewrite has already reached its own floor (the block's product must still cross one adder and the enable mux), and the unmodified fltr_compute_* sum is what now pins the period.

This pass therefore keeps the block rewrite exactly as measured (same 14 converted regions, same 42 blocks, same mapping, same soft remainder) and additionally folds the symmetric taps of fltr_compute_* — the same pre-adder identity the block implements, a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c — and balances that sum, in soft logic. Two reasons for soft rather than more blocks, both from the measured numbers: (1) a block takes a DSP tile alone, 253779, while the baseline packs these 8×9 multiplies about 3.6 to a tile (~70k each), so a block per fold in fltr_compute raises area by roughly 4% with no path shortened; (2) folding removes three of seven products and three of six 20-bit adders per instance, so the soft form is smaller than what it replaces — the 58 DSP tiles the fltr_compute_* multiplies occupy today disappear, leaving the 42 blocks as the design's only DSP tiles, while the fltr_compute path falls from six levels (6.90 ns) to a pre-add plus at most three shift-add levels into the q stage (~4.6 ns) and two levels into d_out_tmp (~2.4 ns). I state plainly that the fltr_compute edit is not itself a block conversion: it is the change that lets the block rewrite's shorter path set the period, and it is area-negative on its own. The arithmetic of those multiplies is kept exactly, term for term, as set out below.

Why Part 1 is exact (unchanged from the measured candidate, which simulated clean). Folding is exact over the integers and each module's coefficient set is symmetric (f1 29/29, 101/101, 15/15; f2 and h2 4/4, 42/42, 163/163; f3 12/12, 77/77, 148/148; h1 15/15, 25/25, 193/193; h3 and h4 9/9, 56/56, 109/109), the centre tap handled separately (235·x3 in f1, 255·x3 in f2/h2; the other four have coefficient 0 there and the original statement omits n_delay_reg3, as does the rewrite). Block limits: each tap is 16-bit unsigned (WIDTH_5B = 16), so A,D ≤ 65535 (within the 25 unsigned bits allowed) and D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit pre-adder sum is 0 and it reads as a positive signed value; each B (101, 163, 77, 193, 109) ≤ 255 with a zero top bit; PCIN = 0 so P = (D+A)·B exactly (largest 193·131070 = 25,296,510, far inside 48 bits). Every soft term is sized to its exact range with all operands unsigned and all results non-negative, so no shift, subtraction or assignment wraps: 3·s0 ≤ 393,210 < 2^19; 32·s0 ≤ 4,194,240 and 29·s0 ≤ 3,801,030 < 2^22; 15·s2 ≤ 1,966,050 < 2^21; 240·x3 ≤ 15,728,400 and 235·x3 ≤ 15,400,725 < 2^24; 4·s0 ≤ 524,280 < 2^19; 40·s1 ≤ 5,242,800 and 42·s1 ≤ 5,504,940 < 2^23; 255·x3 ≤ 16,711,425 < 2^24; 12·s0 ≤ 1,572,840 < 2^21; 144·s2 ≤ 18,874,080 and 148·s2 ≤ 19,398,360 < 2^25; 24·s1 ≤ 3,145,680 and 25·s1 ≤ 3,276,750 < 2^22; 9·s0 ≤ 1,179,630 < 2^21; 64·s1 ≤ 8,388,480 and 56·s1 ≤ 7,339,920 < 2^23; each subtraction has a non-negative result. Module totals (f1 65535·525 = 34,405,875; f2/h2 44,105,055; f3 31,063,590; h1 30,539,310; h3/h4 22,806,180) are below 2^28, so the 28-bit dout assignment truncates nothing, exactly as in the original. The taps keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; nothing but dout reads the products; PCOUT drives nothing; no register is added, moved or removed.

Why Part 2 is exact.

  • What the original computes: q_i is a 17-bit register holding (b_i·c_i) mod 2^17; d_out_tmp (20 bits) is the sum of the seven q_i sign-extended to 20 bits, modulo 2^20; dout is d_out_tmp[18:3].
  • Folding is exact only where no q wraps. For any coefficient c ≤ 255 and byte b ≤ 255, b·c ≤ 65,025 < 2^16, so q[16] = 0 and the sign-extended term equals the plain product. Every folded coefficient here is ≤ 255 (29, 101, 17, 4, 42, 163, 20, 179, 25, 193, 23, 72, 147, 14, 43, 80), so sext20(q_i) + sext20(q_j) = c·b_i + c·b_j = c·(b_i+b_j) exactly, and the folded product is held in a register sized to its maximum (largest 193·510 = 98,430 < 2^17), so nothing truncates.
  • The three coefficients above 255 are kept per-tap, unfolded, so their wrap is reproduced bit for bit: 277·b4 ≤ 70,635, 324·b4 ≤ 82,620, 364·b ≤ 92,820, all < 2^17, so a 17-bit register holds the product exactly, just as * assigned to reg[16:0] does, and the same {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} sign extension is kept — the term goes negative for exactly the same bytes as in the original (b4 ≥ 237 for 277, b4 ≥ 203 for 324, b ≥ 181 for 364). This is why f3's 364 pair is not folded.
  • Shift-add forms are literal identities: 29 = 32−3, 101 = 96+5, 17 = 16+1, 277 = 272+5, 4, 42 = 40+2, 163 = 160+3, 255 = 256−1, 20 = 16+4, 179 = 192−13, 13 = 16−3, 364 = 384−20, 25 = 24+1, 193 = 192+1, 23 = 24−1, 72 = 64+8, 147 = 144+3, 14 = 16−2, 43 = 40+3, 80 = 64+16, 324 = 320+4. Each wire is declared wide enough for its maximum (listed above against each line's comment: 3·s ≤ 1530 in 11 bits; 29·s ≤ 14,790 and 32·s ≤ 16,320 in 14 bits; 96·s ≤ 48,960 and 101·s ≤ 51,510 in 16 bits; 17·s ≤ 8,670 in 14; 272·b ≤ 69,360 and 277·b ≤ 70,635 in 17; 4·s ≤ 2,040 in 11; 40·s ≤ 20,400 and 42·s ≤ 21,420 in 15; 160·s ≤ 81,600 and 163·s ≤ 83,130 in 17; 255·b ≤ 65,025 in 17; 20·s ≤ 10,200 in 14; 13·s ≤ 6,630 in 13; 192·s ≤ 97,920 and 179·s ≤ 91,290 in 17; 384·b ≤ 97,920 and 364·b ≤ 92,820 in 17; 24·s ≤ 12,240 and 25·s ≤ 12,750 in 14; 193·s ≤ 98,430 in 17; 23·s ≤ 11,730 in 14; 72·s ≤ 36,720 in 16; 144·s ≤ 73,440 and 147·s ≤ 74,970 in 17; 14·s ≤ 7,140 in 13; 43·s ≤ 21,930 in 15; 80·s ≤ 40,800 in 16; 320·b ≤ 81,600 and 324·b ≤ 82,620 in 17). Every subtraction has a non-negative result, so no borrow leaves a declared width, and each pair sum sa,sb,sc ≤ 510 fits its 9 bits.
  • The reduction is the same value. All four (or three) terms are 20-bit patterns identical to the ones the original adds — the folded pairs zero-extended (their true values are non-negative and sign bit 0 in the original), the unfolded big-coefficient taps sign-extended exactly as written at lines 867/936/1073. The d_out_tmp context is 20 bits, so every add is modulo 2^20, and addition modulo 2^20 is associative and commutative: re-grouping the seven original terms into three or four pre-summed terms in a balanced tree gives the identical 20-bit result, whether or not the mathematical sum is negative (f3 is the only module where it can be, and it wraps the same way in both versions). dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3] is untouched.
  • Dropped zero terms. In f3, h1 and h3 the original centre multiply is din[31:24] * 16'b0, so q4 is 0 from the first clock edge and every edge after (and the task's premise is that every original register starts at 0), so omitting that term and its register changes no value at any cycle, including after any reset.
  • Visibility. q1..q7 are read only in the d_out_tmp expression of their own module (lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073) and d_out_tmp only in the dout line; din is a module input driven by the fifo* output registers (lines 698-712) and is still read as before. All new wires are internal and read only inside the module.
  • Registers and reset. The stage structure is unchanged: the folded and per-tap products are registered in the same always @(posedge clk) block that held q1..q7, d_out_tmp in the next stage, dout after that. No register is added beyond replacing q1..q7 with the folded set, none is moved across logic, and none of the rewrite's registers is read before it is first written, so behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged. No ASSUMES: line is needed; the match holds on every input value, so it also holds on the reference testbench's stimulus.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region. Before: din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After: the same operands → one combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma (pre-add and multiply) in parallel with the combinational soft pair-adds and shift-add tree → one final combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. Unchanged in every converted module. (For the non-converted fltr_compute_* arithmetic, likewise unchanged: three register stages from din to dout, product stage → d_out_tmp → dout.)

Candidates: converted and left.

  • Converted (14 ids, 42 blocks): the seven folded pairs listed in REGIONS — one per my_fir_* module, carrying that module's most expensive coefficient (101, 163, 77, 193, 163, 109, 109). One block per module is also the minimum that lets the whole module be restructured: an untouched my_fir_* module's seven 16×9 multiplies pack only about 1.5 to a tile (174 tiles for 258 such multiplies at baseline), far more area than one block plus soft shift-adds.
  • Left, in the my_fir_* modules (28 ids): every other tap of f1 (×29 at 1486$154 and 1492$165, ×15 at 1488$157 and 1490$161, ×235 at 1489$159), f2/h2 (×4 at 1542$169, 1548$180, 1716$210, 1722$221; ×42 at 1543$170, 1547$178, 1717$211, 1721$219; ×255 at 1545$174, 1719$215), f3 (×12 at 1602$184, 1607$193; ×148 at 1604$187, 1605$189), h1 (×15 at 1661$197, 1666$206; ×25 at 1662$198, 1665$204), h3/h4 (×9 at 1775$225, 1780$234, 1833$238, 1838$247; ×56 at 1776$226, 1779$232, 1834$239, 1837$245). Reason, common to all: their coefficients are at most two shift-add levels past the folded pair sum, so in soft logic they reach the reduction no later than a block's product (which arrives ~3.87 ns after the clock edge: 1.63 ns of route plus the block's 2.14 ns), while each would cost a whole DSP tile, 253779 — 9.1 CLBs. Their arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same dout sum.
  • Left, in the fltr_compute_* modules (all 46 ids, fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen for the block this pass, for a cost reason, not a correctness one. These 8×9 products pack about 3.6 to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles at baseline, ~70k each), so a block per fold would multiply their area by roughly 3.6× and shorten no path — after the fold their longest path is about 4.6 ns against the my_fir block path's ~6.7 ns. They are kept off the block and folded in soft logic as described in Part 2; their arithmetic is preserved term for term. Within that set, the three ×364 products (f3 …$74, …$76) and the ×277 (f1 …$47) and ×324 (h4 …$131) products are additionally not folded at all, because their results exceed 2^16 and the 17-bit q register is re-read as signed (lines 867, 936, 1073): folding them would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per term. They keep their own 17-bit registers and sign extension. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates; their always-zero terms are dropped as shown.

Resource note. After this edit the design's only DSP tiles are the 42 blocks; the fltr_compute_* multiplies no longer occupy any (58 tiles at the kept candidate's packing), while the folding also removes three of the six 20-bit adders in each of the 42 fltr_compute instances. Expect about 42 DSP tiles packed at seed 1.

DESIGN_CHANGE: two changes to the design itself would let more of it use the block. (1) If fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed the 17-bit qs as unsigned rather than sign-extending them), the ×277, ×324 and ×364 taps could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic. (2) In each v_fltr_*x7, inst_fltr_compute_f2 and inst_fltr_compute_h2 are given the same din and the same coefficients (4,42,163,255,163,42,4), so their outputs are identical every cycle; one of the two could drive both vidin_out_f2 and vidin_out_h2, removing a seventh of that family's arithmetic outright.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: dsp48e2_preadd_ma (precision INT27)
  • what it is: this mode copies the AMD DSP48E2 block in one configuration, "pre-adder multiply on the P cascade, PREG = 0" (UG579 v1.7 Equation 2-2 (p36), pre-adder p35, PCIN/PCOUT p33 and Table 2-6 (p28); the "27x18 + C Systolic MultAdd" rows of Tables 2-13 to 2-17 name the cascaded filter, here without the systolic registers). It is not the whole DSP48E2: only the ports below exist, and the rest of the real block is fixed inside the mode (INMODE = 00100 (D enabled, add), OPMODE = 000010101 (W = 0, Z = PCIN, X and Y = M), ALUMODE = 0000, CARRYINSEL = 000, CARRYIN = 0, C = 0, every clock enable and reset not listed as a port 0). Differences from the real block: one slice per tile where AMD's tile has two; INMODE and OPMODE are fixed inside the mode: add only, no subtract, no C; A is 27 bits; ACOUT, BCOUT and the carry, pattern-detect and XOR outputs are not exposed; the cascade uses the tile's 64-bit chain wires, 48 bits of them; timing figures and tile area are this project's, not AMD's.
  • computes: P = (D + A)*B + PCIN.
  • input ports: A[27], D[27], B[18], PCIN[48]
  • output ports: P[48], PCOUT[48]
  • arithmetic: the block's operands and result are signed two's complement. A design operand narrower than its port must be widened to the port width: zero-extended if the design treats it as unsigned, sign-extended if signed. For unsigned data the top bit of B and of the pre-adder sum D + A must be zero (UG579 p36: "The multiplier can emulate unsigned math by setting the MSB of an input operand to zero."; p35: "limit input operands to 26-bit (or 17-bit for the B path)"). So an unsigned operand may be at most 25 bits on A, 25 bits on D and 17 bits on B; a wider unsigned operand has no exact representation on this block. A and D of at most 25 unsigned bits keep D + A within 26 bits; the 27-bit pre-adder sum wraps and is read as signed. PCIN and P are 48-bit values added modulo 2^48. The result wraps at 48 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 48 bits (modulo 2^48), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and P and PCOUT are valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • cascade: PCOUT is combinational: PCOUT = P in the same cycle, so a cascade of blocks is one combinational path through every block. PCOUT reaches only the PCIN of the block directly below it in the column, by a dedicated wire; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it. PCIN takes only another block's PCOUT, or the constant 0.
  • tie-off: PCIN = 0 when the block is the first of a cascade or is not cascaded (a dedicated cascade input: only another block's PCOUT or the constant 0 may drive it).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.

  • The block has no output register, so the logic its output drives is in the same stage.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's PCOUT can drive the next block's PCIN directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
  • The device has 306 DSP tiles.
  • One DSP tile's area is 253779 minimum-width transistor areas and one CLB's 27905.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. The block has no reset: "same behavior" must hold after every reset of the design, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original on the testbench's stimulus, which does not respect it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left: a correctness reason, or "not chosen this pass"; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically, and your reply is read by the framework, not answered by a person, so do not end with a question or an offer.

  • my_fir_h2: .A({11'b0,n_delay_reg2}) .D({11'b0,n_delay_reg4}) .B(18'd163) .PCIN(48'd0) .P(p163) .PCOUT(); dout <= p163[27:0] + soft;
  • my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4: .A({11'b0,n_delay_reg2}) .D({11'b0,n_delay_reg4}) .B(18'd109) .PCIN(48'd0) .P(p109) .PCOUT(); dout <= p109[27:0] + soft;

PLAN:

What changes from the kept candidate (revision 2), and why. Revision 2 measured 8.003 ns with 78 blocks. Its reported path is: flop 0.103 → 1.627 ns of wire → block 2.140 → add 1.070 → add 1.110 → new_data_rdy enable mux 1.960. Two numbers decide this pass. (1) A block leaf becomes available 3.87 ns after the clock edge, and every block product must still pass through at least one soft adder (1.05 ns) and the enable mux (1.96 ns): the floor for a module with one block is ≈ 6.9 ns, and a module with two block products pays an extra adder level to merge them, pinning it at ≈ 7.9-8.0 ns. That is exactly where revision 2 sits. (2) Counting constant multiplies by CSD tree depth rather than by number of adds, every coefficient in these filters is at most two adder levels past the folded pair sum: 101={64,32,4,1}, 163={128,32,2,1}, 235={256,−16,−4,−1}, 77={64,8,4,1}, 109={128,−16,−2,−1} are 4 terms = 2 levels; 29={32,−2,−1}, 42={32,8,2}, 148={128,16,4}, 193={128,64,1}, 25={16,8,1} are 3 terms = 2 levels; 15, 12, 9, 56, 255 are 1 level; 4 is a wire. So a folded soft product lands at ≈ 0.1 + 3×1.0 = 3.2 ns, i.e. earlier than a block product, and a whole module's soft remainder lands at 4 levels ≈ 3.9-4.7 ns, i.e. about the same time as a block product.

Therefore this pass goes to exactly one block per my_fir_* module, carrying the most expensive coefficient (the one with the most CSD terms, which also removes the most soft adders), with every other tap product computed in soft shift-add logic and merged into a single soft value that meets the block product at the final adder. Each module then has the shape dout <= P + soft: one adder level after the block instead of two. Blocks fall from 78 to 42 (−36 DSP tiles, −9.1e6 area units) against roughly 108 added adders of about 22 bits over all 42 module instances (on the order of +4e6), so area should fall by about 7% while the my_fir critical path loses one adder level (≈ −1.0 ns) if the soft trees meet the block, and is unchanged in the worst case. Downside is bounded: if soft levels turn out to cost ~1.3 ns the period returns to about today's and the loop keeps revision 2.

Editor instructions.

  • Work from the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory; the kept candidate's edit is not present in it. Do not edit any other file and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma.
  • In each of the seven my_fir_* modules, replace only the dout <= ... product-sum statement inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) with the single statement given below. Leave the delay-chain assignments, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, the port list, the register declarations and all COEF* defines exactly as they are. n_delay_reg3 stays in the delay chain of f3/h1/h3/h4 even though nothing reads it there, as in the original.
  • Declare the wires at module level with exactly the widths given (they are chosen so that no intermediate value wraps and no assignment truncates; the LHS width sets the self-determined context of each expression, so do not narrow them), write the assigns as continuous assignments outside the always block, and instantiate the block outside the always block with named connections only. Every input port is connected; PCIN is tied to the constant 48'd0 on every block, which is permitted for a block that is not cascaded; no PCOUT is read.
  • Touch no other module.

Per module (x0 = din, x1..x6 = n_delay_reg1..6):

my_fir_f1 (29,101,15,235,15,101,29) — block ×101 on (x1,x5):

wire [47:0] p101; wire [16:0] s0, s2; wire [18:0] a3, g5;
wire [21:0] t29;  wire [20:0] t15;    wire [23:0] g240, t235;
wire [24:0] w;    wire [25:0] soft;
assign s0   = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};
assign s2   = {1'b0, n_delay_reg2} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg4};
assign a3   = {s0, 1'b0} + s0;                 // 3*s0
assign t29  = {s0, 5'b00000} - a3;             // 29*s0
assign t15  = {s2, 4'b0000} - s2;              // 15*s2
assign g240 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b00000000} - {n_delay_reg3, 4'b0000};
assign g5   = {n_delay_reg3, 2'b00} + n_delay_reg3;
assign t235 = g240 - g5;                       // 235*x3
assign w    = t15 + t235;
assign soft = t29 + w;
dout <= p101[27:0] + soft;

my_fir_f2 (4,42,163,255,163,42,4) — block ×163 on (x2,x4):

wire [47:0] p163; wire [16:0] s0, s1; wire [18:0] t4;
wire [22:0] g40, t42; wire [23:0] t255; wire [24:0] v; wire [25:0] soft;
assign s0   = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};
assign s1   = {1'b0, n_delay_reg1} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg5};
assign t4   = {s0, 2'b00};
assign g40  = {s1, 5'b00000} + {s1, 3'b000};
assign t42  = g40 + {s1, 1'b0};
assign t255 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b00000000} - {8'b00000000, n_delay_reg3};
assign v    = t4 + t255;
assign soft = t42 + v;
dout <= p163[27:0] + soft;

my_fir_h2: identical to my_fir_f2 (same coefficients 4,42,163,255,163,42,4).

my_fir_f3 (12,77,148,0,148,77,12) — block ×77 on (x1,x5):

wire [47:0] p77; wire [16:0] s0, s2; wire [20:0] t12;
wire [24:0] g144, t148; wire [25:0] soft;
assign s0   = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};
assign s2   = {1'b0, n_delay_reg2} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg4};
assign t12  = {s0, 3'b000} + {s0, 2'b00};
assign g144 = {s2, 7'b0000000} + {s2, 4'b0000};
assign t148 = g144 + {s2, 2'b00};
assign soft = t12 + t148;
dout <= p77[27:0] + soft;

my_fir_h1 (15,25,193,0,193,25,15) — block ×193 on (x2,x4):

wire [47:0] p193; wire [16:0] s0, s1; wire [20:0] t15;
wire [21:0] g24, t25; wire [22:0] soft;
assign s0   = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};
assign s1   = {1'b0, n_delay_reg1} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg5};
assign t15  = {s0, 4'b0000} - s0;
assign g24  = {s1, 4'b0000} + {s1, 3'b000};
assign t25  = g24 + s1;
assign soft = t15 + t25;
dout <= p193[27:0] + soft;

my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0,109,56,9) — block ×109 on (x2,x4):

wire [47:0] p109; wire [16:0] s0, s1; wire [20:0] t9;
wire [22:0] t56;  wire [23:0] soft;
assign s0   = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};
assign s1   = {1'b0, n_delay_reg1} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg5};
assign t9   = {s0, 3'b000} + s0;
assign t56  = {s1, 6'b000000} - {s1, 3'b000};
assign soft = t9 + t56;
dout <= p109[27:0] + soft;

Why this is exact.

  • Folding is exact over the integers: a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c, and each module's coefficient set is symmetric (f1 29/29, 101/101, 15/15; f2 and h2 4/4, 42/42, 163/163; f3 12/12, 77/77, 148/148; h1 15/15, 25/25, 193/193; h3 and h4 9/9, 56/56, 109/109), with the centre tap handled separately (235·x3 in f1, 255·x3 in f2/h2; f3, h1, h3, h4 have coefficient 0 there and the original statement omits n_delay_reg3 — my rewrite omits it too).
  • Block operand limits: every tap is 16-bit unsigned (WIDTH_5B = 16), so A, D ≤ 65535, within the 25 unsigned bits allowed; the pre-adder sum D + A ≤ 131070 < 2^26, so bit 26 of the 27-bit sum is 0 and the sum reads as a positive signed value; each B (101, 163, 77, 193, 109) is ≤ 255 with a zero top bit. PCIN = 0, so P = (D+A)*B exactly, far inside 48 bits (largest 193·131070 = 25,296,510).
  • Soft terms, each sized to its exact range, all operands unsigned and all results non-negative, so no shift, subtraction or assignment wraps: 3·s0 ≤ 393,210 < 2^19; 29·s0 ≤ 3,801,030 < 2^22 (and 32·s0 ≤ 4,194,240 < 2^22); 15·s2 ≤ 1,966,050 < 2^21; 240·x3 ≤ 15,728,400 < 2^24; 5·x3 ≤ 327,675 < 2^19; 235·x3 ≤ 15,400,725 < 2^24; 4·s0 ≤ 524,280 < 2^19; 40·s1 ≤ 5,242,800 and 42·s1 ≤ 5,504,940 < 2^23; 255·x3 ≤ 16,711,425 < 2^24; 12·s0 ≤ 1,572,840 < 2^21; 144·s2 ≤ 18,874,080 and 148·s2 ≤ 19,398,360 < 2^25; 24·s1 ≤ 3,145,680 and 25·s1 ≤ 3,276,750 < 2^22; 9·s0 ≤ 1,179,630 < 2^21; 64·s1 ≤ 8,388,480 and 56·s1 ≤ 7,339,920 < 2^23. Every subtraction (32s0−3s0, 16s2−s2, 256x3−16x3, 240x3−5x3, 256x3−x3, 16s0−s0, 64s1−8s1) has a non-negative result, so no borrow leaves the declared width.
  • Partial sums and totals: f1 w ≤ 17,366,775 and soft ≤ 21,167,805 (< 2^25); f2/h2 v ≤ 17,235,705 and soft ≤ 22,740,645; f3 soft ≤ 20,971,200; h1 soft ≤ 5,242,800; h3/h4 soft ≤ 8,519,550. Module totals: f1 65535·525 = 34,405,875; f2/h2 65535·673 = 44,105,055; f3 65535·474 = 31,063,590; h1 65535·466 = 30,539,310; h3/h4 65535·348 = 22,806,180 — all below 2^28, so the 28-bit dout assignment truncates nothing, exactly as in the original (which also assigns this sum to the 28-bit dout). All wires are unsigned, so every addend is zero-extended into the 28-bit context of the dout assignment. The rewrite matches bit for bit on every input value; no ASSUMES: line is needed and the match does not depend on the testbench's stimulus.
  • Visibility: the taps din and n_delay_reg1..6 keep their own registers and are still read by the delay chain outside the blocks; only the products, which nothing else in the design reads (dout is the only other value, and it is unchanged), move inside a block or into the soft terms. The pre-adder sums and all t*/g*/soft wires are new internal values that nothing else reads. PCOUT drives nothing, as required for a block whose output must stay on general routing.
  • Registers and reset: the block has no register and the rewrite adds none — every new wire is combinational. No register is added, moved or removed, so behaviour after every reset of the design is unchanged and nothing depends on an unknown start-up value.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region: before — din/n_delay_reg1..6 → combinational constant multiply → combinational 28-bit adder tree → the dout register, clock-enabled by new_data_rdy: one register stage. After — the same operands → one combinational dsp48e2_preadd_ma (pre-add and multiply) in parallel with the combinational soft pair-adds and shift-add tree → one final combinational 28-bit add → the same dout register with the same enable: one register stage. Unchanged in every converted module.

Per-module leaf arrival and tree shape. Soft values ready one adder level after the taps (the pair sums s0, s1, s2 and the x3 partials) are reduced by a balanced tree so that soft is ready in 3 further levels for f1 (7 level-1 values), f2/h2 (5), f3 (5), h1 (5), and in 2 further levels for h3/h4 (4). The block product (≈3.87 ns measured) then meets soft at a single final adder, so the block passes through exactly one adder level in every module — against two levels in revision 2 for f1, f2, f3, h1, h2.

Candidates left, and why.

  • Left because the folded pair's (or centre tap's) coefficient is cheap in soft logic — at most two adder levels past the pair sum, so it reaches the reduction no later than a block product would, while a block would cost a whole DSP tile (9.1 CLBs). Their arithmetic is kept exactly, as terms of the same dout sum: my_fir_f1.$mul$…1486$154, …1492$165 (×29), …1488$157, …1490$161 (×15), …1489$159 (×235); my_fir_f2.$mul$…1542$169, …1548$180, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1716$210, …1722$221 (×4), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1543$170, …1547$178, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1717$211, …1721$219 (×42), my_fir_f2.$mul$…1545$174, my_fir_h2.$mul$…1719$215 (×255); my_fir_f3.$mul$…1602$184, …1607$193 (×12), …1604$187, …1605$189 (×148); my_fir_h1.$mul$…1661$197, …1666$206 (×15), …1662$198, …1665$204 (×25); my_fir_h3.$mul$…1775$225, …1780$234, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1833$238, …1838$247 (×9), my_fir_h3.$mul$…1776$226, …1779$232, my_fir_h4.$mul$…1834$239, …1837$245 (×56).
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1.$mul$…$44 through fltr_compute_h4.$mul$…$134): not chosen this pass, for two reasons, neither a correctness block. (1) At baseline these 8-bit × 9-bit products pack four to a tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt (210 multiplies on 62 tiles); this mode takes a whole tile per block, so folding their symmetric pairs would need about 4 blocks per module instance, 150+ tiles where 62 are used now — the opposite of this pass's direction — and moving them to soft logic instead costs more CLB area than the 62 tiles it frees (≈12 shift-adders per instance over 42 instances). (2) Each q1..q7 is a 17-bit register re-read as signed ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), so a product that reaches 2^16 contributes −2^17 to d_out_tmp; with din bytes up to 255 that happens for coefficients above 257 — 277 (f1 q4), 364 (f3 q3/q5), 324 (h4 q4) — and an exact rewrite would need a comparator and a −2^17 correction per such term plus a restructuring of the q/d_out_tmp two-stage pipeline. The three * 16'b0…0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) are not candidates and are untouched.

Resource check. 42 blocks plus the untouched fltr_compute_* multiplies (62 tiles at baseline, 57 as packed in revision 1) is about 99 of the 306 DSP tiles, 39 fewer than revision 2's 138 — a compaction that should also shorten the 1.63 ns flop-to-A route and the 1.81 ns route into the enable mux.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute_* held its tap products in 20-bit unsigned registers (or summed them as unsigned instead of sign-extending the 17-bit q), its symmetric pairs could fold onto the pre-adder with no correction logic; and if its q stage were replaced by a registered copy of din, those products would become a single combinational stage like the my_fir_* family.

The plan

I'll read the source first.

REGIONS: my_fir_f1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1487$155, my_fir_f1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1491$163, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1544$172, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1546$176, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1603$185, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1606$191, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1663$200, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1664$202, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1718$213, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1720$217, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1777$228, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1778$230, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1835$241, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1836$243
SHARED_REDUCTION: the dout register of each my_fir_* module (one reduction per module: the block's P added to one soft-computed sum of the remaining taps; no PCOUT→PCIN cascade)
BLOCKS: 42 (7 instantiations written in the source, one per my_fir_* module; each module has 6 instances)
MAPPING: one block per my_fir_* module, exactly as in the kept candidate. In every block A and D carry a 16-bit unsigned tap zero-extended to 27 bits ({11'b0, tap}), B carries that folded pair's coefficient as 18'd<c> (top bit 0), PCIN is 48'd0 (not cascaded), P is read as P[27:0], PCOUT is left unconnected and read by nothing. Taps: x0 = din, x1..x6 = n_delay_reg1..6.

  • my_fir_f1: .A({11'b0,n_delay_reg1}) .D({11'b0,n_delay_reg5}) .B(18'd101) .PCIN(48'd0) .P(p101) .PCOUT(); dout <= p101[27:0] + soft;
  • my_fir_f2: .A({11'b0,n_delay_reg2}) .D({11'b0,n_delay_reg4}) .B(18'd163) .PCIN(48'd0) .P(p163) .PCOUT(); dout <= p163[27:0] + soft;
  • my_fir_f3: .A({11'b0,n_delay_reg1}) .D({11'b0,n_delay_reg5}) .B(18'd77) .PCIN(48'd0) .P(p77) .PCOUT(); dout <= p77[27:0] + soft;
  • my_fir_h1: .A({11'b0,n_delay_reg2}) .D({11'b0,n_delay_reg4}) .B(18'd193) .PCIN(48'd0) .P(p193) .PCOUT(); dout <= p193[27:0] + soft;
  • my_fir_h2: .A({11'b0,n_delay_reg2}) .D({11'b0,n_delay_reg4}) .B(18'd163) .PCIN(48'd0) .P(p163) .PCOUT(); dout <= p163[27:0] + soft;
  • my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4: .A({11'b0,n_delay_reg2}) .D({11'b0,n_delay_reg4}) .B(18'd109) .PCIN(48'd0) .P(p109) .PCOUT(); dout <= p109[27:0] + soft;

PLAN:

What this pass changes, and why. The kept candidate's own timing report settles where the period now comes from. Its worst path is six chained adders from a latch to a plain flip-flop with no clock-enable multiplexer at the end (lo14351.Q → $add~1795 … $add~1800 → $dff~1816^Q~18, 6.8997 ns). The only six-deep adder chain in this design that ends at an unguarded register is d_out_tmp <= q1+q2+q3+q4+q5+q6+q7 in the seven fltr_compute_* modules (lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073): seven sign-extended 20-bit terms, left-associative, six ripple adds, ~1.13 ns per level, and d_out_tmp has no enable. Every my_fir_* path, by contrast, must end in the new_data_rdy enable mux, which the earlier revision-2 report shows explicitly (1.960 ns); revision 2's my_fir path was 0.103 + 1.627 (route to A) + 2.140 (block) + 1.070 + 1.110 + 1.960 = 8.01 ns, and removing one adder level gave revision 4's my_fir shape at about 6.7 ns — at or just under the measured worst. So the my_fir_* block rewrite has already reached its own floor (the block's product must still cross one adder and the enable mux), and the unmodified fltr_compute_* sum is what now pins the period.

This pass therefore keeps the block rewrite exactly as measured (same 14 converted regions, same 42 blocks, same mapping, same soft remainder) and additionally folds the symmetric taps of fltr_compute_* — the same pre-adder identity the block implements, a*c + b*c = (a+b)*c — and balances that sum, in soft logic. Two reasons for soft rather than more blocks, both from the measured numbers: (1) a block takes a DSP tile alone, 253779, while the baseline packs these 8×9 multiplies about 3.6 to a tile (~70k each), so a block per fold in fltr_compute raises area by roughly 4% with no path shortened; (2) folding removes three of seven products and three of six 20-bit adders per instance, so the soft form is smaller than what it replaces — the 58 DSP tiles the fltr_compute_* multiplies occupy today disappear, leaving the 42 blocks as the design's only DSP tiles, while the fltr_compute path falls from six levels (6.90 ns) to a pre-add plus at most three shift-add levels into the q stage (~4.6 ns) and two levels into d_out_tmp (~2.4 ns). I state plainly that the fltr_compute edit is not itself a block conversion: it is the change that lets the block rewrite's shorter path set the period, and it is area-negative on its own. The arithmetic of those multiplies is kept exactly, term for term, as set out below.

Editor instructions.

  • Work from the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory; no earlier edit is present in it. Do not edit any other file and do not add a module definition for dsp48e2_preadd_ma.
  • Declare every wire at module level with exactly the widths given (they are chosen so that no intermediate wraps and no assignment truncates; the LHS width sets the self-determined context of each expression, so do not narrow or widen them), write the assigns as continuous assignments outside the always block, and instantiate blocks outside the always block with named connections only.
  • Touch only the seven my_fir_* modules and the seven fltr_compute_* modules. Leave port lists, COEF* defines, the new_data_rdy guard, output_data_ready, the else branch, and the delay-chain assignments as they are.
